name: Croissant
description: Buttery, flaky laminated pastry with a golden crust and pillowy interior.

components.name: egg wash
components.comment: beaten whole egg; amount used for brushing

components.name: butter
components.comment: 20 g for the dough; 80 g for lamination

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, milk, sugar, salt and 20 g softened butter into a smooth dough. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Flatten the remaining 80 g cold butter between sheets of baking paper into a small square. Chill until firm but pliable.
Roll the dough around the butter to enclose it. Roll into a rectangle and fold in thirds. Chill for 30 minutes. Repeat the rolling, folding and chilling 3 more times, keeping the butter cold.
Roll the dough about 4 mm thick and cut into 6 long triangles. Roll each triangle from its base to its tip and place on a lined baking tray.
Leave to proof for about 2 hours at room temperature, until visibly puffy. The butter should not melt during proofing.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Brush with 10 g beaten egg and bake for 15–18 minutes, until deeply golden. Makes 6 small croissants.

name: Minestrone Soup
description: Rustic Italian vegetable soup with tomatoes, zucchini, beans, and pasta.

components.name: olive oil
components.comment: 15 ml for cooking; 5 ml for serving

steps.text: Dice the onion, carrot and celery. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a pot and cook the vegetables for 8 minutes. Add chopped garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the canned tomatoes and vegetable stock and bring to a boil.
Add diced zucchini and the drained canned beans. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the dry pasta and cook for the time stated on its packet, usually 8–10 minutes. Add a little water if the soup becomes too thick.
Stir in chopped basil, salt and pepper. Divide into 4 bowls and finish with the remaining 5 ml olive oil. Extra bread is optional and is not included in the recipe quantities.

name: French Fries
description: Golden crispy potato fries seasoned with sea salt — the ultimate side dish.

steps.text: Peel and cut potatoes into even sticks. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes to remove starch.
Drain and dry very thoroughly — water causes dangerous oil splashing.
First fry at 160°C for 5 minutes (blanching). Remove and drain. They should not be golden yet.
Heat oil to 190°C. Fry again in batches for 2–3 minutes until deeply golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels and season immediately with sea salt. Serve at once.

name: Crème Brûlée
description: Creamy vanilla custard beneath a perfectly crackled caramelised sugar crust.

steps.text: Heat cream with a split vanilla bean until steaming (not boiling). Remove bean.
Whisk egg yolks with sugar until pale. Slowly pour warm cream into yolks, whisking constantly.
Strain the custard and pour into ramekins.
Place ramekins in a water bath. Bake at 150°C for 35–40 minutes until just set but still wobbly.
Cool, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Sprinkle a thin layer of sugar over each ramekin. Caramelise with a blowtorch until amber and crackling.

name: Ajapsandali (Georgian Vegetable Stew)
description: Eggplant, pepper, and tomato stewed together with garlic and herbs — Georgia's everyday summer vegetable dish, made whenever the garden is full.

steps.text: Cut the eggplant, peppers, tomatoes, and onion into bite-sized chunks.
Salt the eggplant and let sit for 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat oil in a wide pan and fry the eggplant until softened and lightly golden, about 8 minutes.
Add the onion and peppers, and cook for another 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, garlic, and khmeli-suneli, cover, and simmer for 12-15 minutes until everything is soft and stewed together.
Season with salt, stir in cilantro, and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Mashed Potatoes
description: Buttery, silky smooth mashed potatoes — the ultimate comfort side dish.

steps.text: Peel and cube potatoes. Cover with cold salted water and bring to a boil.
Cook for 15–20 minutes until completely tender when pierced. Drain thoroughly.
Return to the dry pot over low heat for 1 minute to drive off excess moisture.
Mash with a potato ricer or masher. Do not use a blender — it makes them gluey.
Gradually beat in hot milk and cold butter in stages until silky. Season with salt and a pinch of nutmeg.

name: Gazpacho
description: Ice-cold Spanish blended tomato soup with cucumber, pepper, and sherry vinegar.

steps.text: Roughly chop tomatoes, cucumber, and pepper. Soak a slice of stale bread in water.
Blend all vegetables with garlic, soaked bread, sherry vinegar, and olive oil until smooth.
Season with salt. Add a splash of cold water to adjust consistency.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until very cold. Serve in glasses with diced vegetable garnish.

name: Żurek (Polish Sour Rye Soup)
description: Thick, tangy Polish soup made from fermented rye starter with sausage and hard-boiled egg.

steps.text: Boil white sausage and potatoes in separate pots until cooked through. Slice sausage.
In a pot, combine rye sour base (zakwas) with meat stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add crushed garlic and dried marjoram. Stir in a large spoonful of sour cream.
Add sliced sausage and diced potatoes. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and white pepper. The soup should have a distinct, pleasant sourness.
Serve in deep bowls or hallowed bread rolls, topped with a halved hard-boiled egg.

name: Rote Grütze (Red Berry Pudding)
description: Northern German summer dessert of mixed red berries in a light vanilla sauce.

steps.text: Combine all berries and cherries in a saucepan with sugar and a splash of water.
Heat gently until berries soften and release juice, about 5 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with cold water. Stir into the bubbling berries.
Cook 2–3 minutes until the mixture thickens. Do not overcook — keep it glossy.
Pour into individual glasses. Cool, then refrigerate. Serve with vanilla sauce or cream.

name: Mamaliga with Bryndza
description: Romanian golden polenta served with creamy sheep's milk cheese and sour cream.

steps.text: Bring salted water to a boil. Slowly pour cornmeal in a steady stream, whisking constantly.
Switch to a wooden spoon. Cook on medium heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring frequently, until thick and pulling away from sides.
Remove from heat and stir in butter.
Pour onto a wooden board or plates. Make a well in the centre.
Fill the well with crumbled bryndza cheese. Serve immediately with cold sour cream.

name: Nicoise Salad
description: French composed salad with tuna, soft eggs, green beans, olives, and anchovy.

steps.text: Soft-boil eggs for 7–8 minutes. Cool and halve.
Blanch green beans in boiling salted water for 3 minutes. Plunge into ice water.
Boil new potatoes until tender. Drain and halve while warm.
Make vinaigrette: whisk Dijon mustard, red wine vinegar, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Arrange all ingredients on a platter in separate groups — do not toss. Drape anchovy fillets over.
Drizzle vinaigrette over everything. Serve immediately with crusty bread.

name: Sauerbraten
description: German pot roast marinated in vinegar and spices for days, served with red cabbage.

steps.text: Make marinade: boil vinegar, wine, onion, bay leaf, juniper berries, and cloves. Cool completely.
Submerge beef in marinade in the fridge for 3–5 days, turning daily.
Remove beef and pat dry. Strain and reserve marinade.
Brown beef on all sides in a heavy pot. Add strained marinade.
Braise covered at 160°C for 2.5–3 hours until very tender.
Crumble ginger snap cookies into the braising liquid — they thicken the sauce and add sweetness. Serve sliced with red cabbage.

name: Butter Naan
description: Soft and pillowy Indian flatbread brushed with garlic butter, baked in a hot pan.

steps.text: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt, yogurt, and warm water. Knead into a soft dough. Rest covered for 1 hour.
Divide into balls. Roll each into a teardrop shape about 5 mm thick.
Heat a cast iron pan over maximum heat until very hot.
Place naan in the pan. Cook 1–2 minutes until large bubbles form on the surface.
Flip and cook 1 more minute until charred spots appear.
Brush immediately with garlic butter and scatter fresh cilantro. Serve hot.

name: Käsespätzle
description: German egg noodle dumplings baked with Emmental cheese and crispy fried onion.

steps.text: Cook the prepared spätzle according to the package instructions, then drain well.
Thinly slice the onion and fry it in butter over medium-low heat until deeply golden and caramelised.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Layer the cooked spätzle with grated Emmental in an ovenproof dish.
Bake for about 15 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Top with caramelised onion and chopped chives. Serve with sour cream on the side.

name: Kebab
description: Spiced minced lamb skewers grilled over charcoal with herbs and onion.

steps.text: Combine lamb mince with very finely grated onion, parsley, cumin, paprika, and a pinch of cinnamon.
Knead the mixture firmly for 3–5 minutes until it becomes cohesive and slightly sticky.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes. Shape onto flat metal skewers with wet hands.
Grill over charcoal or a very hot grill pan, turning every 2 minutes for 8–10 minutes total.
Serve with flatbread, sliced onion sprinkled with sumac, and tomato.

name: Trofie al Pesto
description: Ligurian pasta tossed with fresh basil pesto, green beans, and new potatoes.

steps.text: Make pesto: blend basil, pine nuts, garlic, and salt in a processor. Slowly stream in olive oil. Fold in grated Parmesan.
Boil salted water. Add halved new potatoes and cook for 10 minutes.
Add trofie pasta to the same pot. After 3 minutes, add trimmed green beans.
Cook until pasta is al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water. Drain.
Toss everything with pesto and a splash of pasta water to loosen. Serve immediately.

name: Ribeye Steak
description: Pan-seared ribeye basted in butter, garlic, and rosemary until perfectly charred.

steps.text: Take steak out of fridge 30–60 minutes before cooking. Pat dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a cast iron pan over very high heat until almost smoking.
Sear steak for 2–3 minutes per side without moving. For a 3 cm steak: 3 min each side for medium-rare.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter, crushed garlic cloves, and rosemary. Tilt pan and spoon butter over steak continuously for 1–2 minutes.
Rest steak on a warm board for 5–8 minutes. Slice against the grain. Finish with flaky salt.

name: Double Smash Burger
description: Two thin crispy-edged smash patties with caramelised onion and American cheese.

steps.text: Thinly slice the onion and cook in 5 g butter over low heat for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and golden. Add a splash of water if it begins to catch.
Divide the 180 g beef into two loose 90 g balls without compacting them.
Heat a cast-iron pan until very hot. Add the beef balls, spaced apart, and press each firmly into a thin patty.
Season with the measured salt and pepper. Cook until the underside is well browned, about 90 seconds.
Flip each patty, add one slice of cheese and continue cooking until the beef is cooked through.
Toast the split bun. Spread with the sauce and stack both patties, the cooked onion and sliced pickles inside the single bun.

name: New York Cheesecake
description: Dense and creamy baked cheesecake on a buttery graham cracker crust.

steps.text: Crush graham crackers and mix with melted butter. Press into the base of a springform tin. Chill.
Beat cream cheese until smooth. Add sugar, vanilla, sour cream, and mix until silky.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing on low speed — do not over-mix to avoid cracks.
Pour batter over the crust. Wrap the tin base in foil and place in a water bath.
Bake at 160°C for 60–70 minutes until the edges are set but centre still jiggles.
Turn off oven, leave door ajar and let cheesecake cool inside for 1 hour. Then refrigerate overnight.

name: Pierogi Ruskie
description: Polish dumplings stuffed with potato and farmer's cheese, fried in butter with onion.

steps.text: Make dough: combine flour, egg, warm water, and salt. Knead until smooth and elastic. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Boil potatoes until tender. Mash. Mix with farmer's cheese and sautéed onion. Season with salt and pepper.
Roll dough thin. Cut circles with a glass. Place a teaspoon of filling in each, fold and seal tightly.
Boil in salted water for 4–5 minutes after they float. Drain.
Pan-fry boiled pierogi in butter with diced onion until golden and slightly crispy on both sides.
Serve with extra caramelised onion, crispy bacon bits, and sour cream.

name: Tiramisu
description: Silky Italian dessert of espresso-soaked ladyfingers layered with mascarpone cream.

steps.text: Separate eggs. Whisk yolks with sugar until pale and creamy.
Fold mascarpone into the yolk mixture until smooth.
Whip egg whites to stiff peaks and fold gently into the mascarpone mixture.
Brew strong espresso and let it cool. Add a splash of Marsala or rum if desired.
Briefly dip each ladyfinger into the espresso and arrange in a single layer in a dish.
Spread half the mascarpone cream over the ladyfingers. Repeat with a second layer.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight. Dust with cocoa powder before serving.

name: Pasta Aglio e Olio
description: Garlic and olive oil pasta with a kick of chili — the classic late-night, empty-fridge Italian staple.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Thinly slice the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a pan over low heat and gently cook the garlic and chili flakes until golden, not browned.
Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Toss the pasta into the pan with the garlic oil, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen.
Stir through the parsley and serve immediately.

name: Menemen
description: Turkish scrambled eggs cooked with tomatoes, green pepper, and spices.

steps.text: Sauté diced onion and sliced green pepper in olive oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add diced or grated tomatoes. Cook until sauce thickens, about 8 minutes.
Season with paprika and red pepper flakes.
Crack eggs directly into the sauce. Stir gently to scramble into soft, loose curds.
Remove from heat when eggs are just set but still creamy. Serve directly in the pan with bread.

name: Borscht with Beef
description: Hearty Ukrainian borscht slowly simmered with beef, beetroot, and vegetables.

steps.text: Cut the beef into bite-sized pieces. Cover with 1.2 litres water, bring to a boil and skim the surface. Simmer gently for about 1 hour, until the meat is nearly tender.
Grate the beetroot and carrot and dice the onion. Heat the sunflower oil in a separate pan and cook the vegetables for 10 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and vinegar.
Add diced potatoes and shredded cabbage to the beef broth and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the beetroot mixture and simmer for another 10 minutes, until the meat and vegetables are tender. Add a little water if needed to keep a soup consistency.
Stir in the measured sugar, salt and pepper. Divide into 4 bowls and add 20 g sour cream and chopped dill to each portion.

name: Mannaya Kasha (Semolina Porridge)
description: Warm milk semolina porridge, the everyday Russian breakfast most kids grow up eating, sweetened lightly and finished with butter.

steps.text: Bring the milk to a gentle boil in a saucepan with sugar and a pinch of salt.
Lower the heat and slowly stream in the semolina while whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring often, until thickened.
Remove from heat, stir in the butter, and let it stand for 2 minutes before serving.

name: Tarte Tatin
description: Classic French upside-down caramelised apple tart baked under buttery puff pastry.

steps.text: Peel, core, and halve apples.
In an oven-proof skillet, make dry caramel by melting sugar until amber. Add butter and stir.
Pack apple halves tightly, cut-side up, in the caramel. Cook on medium heat for 10 minutes.
Roll puff pastry into a circle. Drape over the apples, tucking edges in around them.
Bake at 200°C for 25–30 minutes until pastry is golden brown.
Cool 5 minutes only — then invert onto a plate immediately. Serve warm with crème fraîche.

name: Chicken Quesadilla
description: Crispy folded tortilla stuffed with grilled chicken, cheese, and peppers.

steps.text: Season chicken with cumin, salt, and pepper. Pan-fry until golden and cooked through. Slice.
Sauté sliced onion and pepper until soft.
Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Place tortilla in pan.
Cover one half with cheese, chicken, and peppers. Fold over the other half.
Cook 2–3 minutes per side until golden and cheese is melted. Cut into wedges and serve with salsa and sour cream.

name: Takoyaki
description: Japanese octopus-filled batter balls topped with mayo and bonito flakes.

steps.text: Make the batter by whisking the takoyaki batter mix with dashi and eggs until smooth.
Heat a takoyaki pan and brush all holes with oil.
Fill each hole to the brim with batter. Place a cube of cooked octopus and a pinch of green onion in each.
When the base sets and edges look cooked, rotate each ball 90 degrees using a skewer. Add more batter if needed to fill gaps.
Continue rotating until the balls are round and golden all over — about 8–10 minutes total.
Serve immediately drizzled with takoyaki sauce, Japanese mayo, bonito flakes, and aonori.

name: Eintopf (German One-Pot)
description: Warming German one-pot stew with pork, root vegetables, and pearl barley.

steps.text: Cut the pork into small cubes. Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the pork for about 10 minutes.
Add chopped carrot, celeriac and leek and cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
Add the dry pearl barley, bay leaf and vegetable stock. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 35 minutes.
Add diced potatoes and simmer for another 20 minutes, until the pork, barley and vegetables are tender. Add a little water if necessary.
Remove the bay leaf. Stir in the measured salt and pepper and scatter with chopped parsley. Divide into 4 portions.

name: Tofu and Veggie Bowl
description: Nourishing bowl of steamed rice, crispy tofu, spinach, avocado, and sesame.

steps.text: Press tofu between paper towels for 10 minutes to remove moisture. Cut into cubes.
Toss tofu in cornstarch, salt, and pepper. Pan-fry in oil until crispy on all sides. Add garlic and soy sauce at the end.
Wilt spinach in the same pan for 1 minute. Season with sesame oil.
Place rice in a bowl. Arrange crispy tofu, wilted spinach, and sliced avocado on top.
Drizzle with soy sauce and sesame oil. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

name: Qofte (Albanian Meatballs)
description: Spiced lamb and beef meatballs grilled over charcoal and served with flatbread.

steps.text: Combine lamb and beef mince with grated onion, minced garlic, fresh mint, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Knead the mixture vigorously for 3 minutes. Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Shape into small oval meatballs or elongated fingers.
Grill on a very hot grill or pan for 3–4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Serve with warm flatbread, plain yogurt, sliced tomato, and onion.

name: Ajvar (Roasted Pepper Relish)
description: Smoky Balkan relish of roasted red peppers and eggplant — eaten on bread or as a side.

steps.text: Roast whole red peppers and eggplant directly over a gas flame or in a hot oven until charred on all sides.
Place in a bowl covered with plastic wrap. Steam for 15 minutes, then peel and remove seeds.
Roughly chop the flesh. Cook in a wide pan with olive oil over medium heat for 30 minutes, stirring.
Add minced garlic and vinegar. Continue cooking until thick and jammy.
Season with salt. Cool and store in jars. Serve on bread, with grilled meats, or as a condiment.

name: Linsensuppe mit Wurst (German Lentil Soup with Sausage)
description: Hearty lentil soup with potato, carrot, and sliced sausage — a filling German one-pot meal (Eintopf) cooked in home kitchens across the country.

steps.text: Rinse the lentils. Dice the potatoes, carrot, and onion.
Combine the lentils, potatoes, carrot, onion, bay leaf, and stock in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils and vegetables are tender.
Meanwhile, slice the sausage and fry it in a separate pan until lightly browned.
Stir the sausage into the soup and simmer for another 5 minutes.
Season with salt and a splash of vinegar to taste, then serve hot with bread.

name: Shashlik (Skewer BBQ)
description: Marinated pork skewers grilled over open fire — the quintessential summer feast.

steps.text: Cut pork neck into 4 cm cubes. Grate onion and combine with vinegar, oil, bay leaf, salt, and spices.
Marinate pork in the mixture for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Thread onto metal skewers alternating with raw onion slices.
Grill over hot charcoal (not open flame) for 15–20 minutes, turning every 3–4 minutes.
Meat should be slightly charred outside and juicy inside. Serve with lavash and fresh vegetables.

name: Pan-Seared Salmon
description: Pan-seared salmon fillet with lemon, rosemary, garlic, and olive oil.

steps.text: Pat the salmon dry and season with the measured salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Place the salmon skin-side down and cook for 4–5 minutes.
Turn the fillets and add the butter, lightly crushed garlic and rosemary. Baste for 2–3 minutes, or until cooked through.
Discard the rosemary stems. Finish with lemon juice and divide between 2 plates. Side dishes are not included in these quantities.

name: Makarony po-Flotski (Navy-Style Pasta)
description: Soviet-era classic of short pasta stirred through with browned ground beef and onion — quick, cheap, and still a weeknight go-to.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente. Drain.
Meanwhile, finely dice the onion.
Heat oil in a pan, fry the onion until soft, then add the beef mince and cook until browned, about 8 minutes.
Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Add the drained pasta and butter to the pan and toss everything together over low heat for 2 minutes.
Serve hot, straight from the pan.

name: Medovik (Honey Cake)
description: Multi-layered Russian honey cake with delicate sponge and thick sour cream frosting.

steps.text: Melt honey and butter in a bain-marie. Add sugar and eggs, stirring constantly. Add baking soda — mixture will foam.
Remove from heat and mix in flour to form a soft dough. Divide into 8 equal portions.
Roll each portion paper-thin on parchment. Bake at 180°C for 3–4 minutes per layer until golden.
Trim each layer to a consistent round using a plate as a guide. Save the trimmings.
Whip sour cream with sugar and vanilla until thick. Spread generously between each layer.
Frost the outside. Crush trimmings into crumbs and coat the top and sides. Refrigerate overnight.

name: Burrito
description: Flour tortilla packed with seasoned chicken, rice, black beans, and sour cream.

steps.text: Season and grill or pan-fry chicken breast until cooked through. Slice into strips.
Warm black beans with a pinch of cumin and salt.
Warm flour tortilla in a dry pan or microwave for 20 seconds to make it pliable.
Layer rice, beans, chicken, salsa, cheese, sour cream, and guacamole in the centre.
Fold the sides in, then roll tightly from the bottom up. Toast seam-side down in a pan for 1–2 minutes to seal.

name: Blini with Red Caviar
description: Thin Russian pancakes topped generously with red salmon caviar and sour cream.

steps.text: Whisk eggs with warm milk, melted butter, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Mix in flour until smooth. Rest batter 15 minutes.
Heat a small crepe pan over medium-high heat. Brush with butter.
Pour a small ladleful and swirl immediately to spread thinly. Cook 60–90 seconds until edges lift.
Flip and cook 30 more seconds. Stack and keep warm.
Serve each blini with a spoonful of cold sour cream and a generous heap of red caviar on top.

name: Grilled Trout
description: Whole trout roasted with herbs, lemon slices, and garlic until flaky and fragrant.

steps.text: Score both sides of the fish with 3 diagonal cuts. Season inside and out with salt and pepper.
Stuff the cavity with lemon slices, garlic, and fresh herbs.
Drizzle generously with olive oil.
Grill on a hot barbecue or under an oven broiler for 5–6 minutes per side.
Fish is done when the skin is crispy and the flesh flakes easily. Serve with lemon and fresh salad.

name: Frijoles con Arroz (Beans and Rice)
description: Simmered beans over steamed rice with a little onion and garlic — the everyday base of a Mexican home meal.

steps.text: Cook the rice according to package instructions.
Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat oil in a pan and cook the onion and garlic until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the beans with their liquid and cumin, and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing some of the beans for texture.
Season with salt, scatter with cilantro, and serve over the rice.

name: Buffalo Chicken Wings
description: Crispy wings tossed in tangy-hot Buffalo sauce and served with blue cheese dip.

steps.text: Pat wings dry. Toss with baking powder, salt, and garlic powder — this is key for crispiness.
Place on a rack over a tray. Bake at 200°C for 45–50 minutes, flipping halfway, until very crispy.
Make Buffalo sauce: melt butter and whisk in hot sauce (Frank's Red Hot) and a splash of vinegar.
Toss hot wings in Buffalo sauce until fully coated. Serve with celery sticks and blue cheese dip.

name: Hungarian Goulash (Bogrács)
description: Hearty paprika-rich beef and potato stew, the soul of Hungarian cuisine.

steps.text: Cut the beef into cubes. Heat the oil in a heavy pot or kettle and brown the beef in batches, about 10 minutes in total. Remove to a plate.
Cook diced onion and pepper in the same pot for 5 minutes. Remove from direct heat and stir in both paprikas.
Return the beef and add tomato paste, caraway seeds, bay leaf and the litre of stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer for 60–70 minutes, until the beef is almost tender.
Add diced potatoes and carrots and cook for another 20 minutes, until tender. Keep a generous amount of broth, adding water if necessary.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in salt and pepper and serve in 4 deep bowls. Extra bread is optional and is not included in the quantities.

name: Pljeskavica (Balkan Burger)
description: Jumbo-sized Balkan spiced beef and lamb patty served in flatbread with kaymak.

steps.text: Mix beef and lamb mince with finely diced onion, paprika, chili flakes, salt, and pepper.
Knead the mixture well and form into a large flat patty, about 2 cm thick.
Grill on a very hot charcoal grill for 4–5 minutes per side.
Warm flatbread. Spread kaymak (or sour cream) on one side and ajvar on the other.
Place pljeskavica in the bread with diced onion and tomato. Serve immediately.

name: Trilece (Balkan Milk Cake)
description: Soft sponge cake soaked in three milks and topped with burnt caramel.

steps.text: Whisk eggs and sugar until very pale and tripled in volume. Fold in flour and baking powder. Pour into a baking tray. Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes.
While still hot, pierce the sponge all over with a fork or skewer.
Mix whole milk, condensed milk, and evaporated milk. Pour very slowly over the hot cake. Refrigerate 4 hours.
Whip heavy cream to stiff peaks. Spread evenly over the soaked cake.
Make dry caramel: melt sugar until dark amber. Quickly pour over cream and tilt tray to spread. Refrigerate until set.
Serve cold in squares.

name: Lahmacun
description: Thin Turkish flatbread topped with spiced minced lamb, tomato, and herbs.

steps.text: Make a simple yeasted dough. Rest 30 minutes and roll paper thin.
Process lamb mince with grated tomato, onion, parsley, cumin, paprika, salt, and chili into a paste.
Spread a very thin layer of meat paste on each flatbread, right to the edges.
Bake in the hottest oven possible (250°C+) for 6–8 minutes until edges crisp and meat is cooked.
Roll up with sliced tomato, parsley, and a squeeze of lemon. Eat with your hands.

name: Çiğ Köfte Wrap
description: Turkish spiced bulgur roll wrapped in lettuce with pomegranate molasses and herbs.

steps.text: Combine fine bulgur with tomato paste and chili paste. Knead for 5 minutes.
Add pomegranate molasses, grated onion, finely chopped parsley, and salt. Knead until smooth.
If mixture is too dry, add a tiny splash of water. It should be firm and hold shape.
Shape into oval patties by squeezing in your fist.
Serve on lettuce leaves with a squeeze of lemon, extra pomegranate molasses, and fresh herbs. Roll up and eat.

name: Draniki (Potato Pancakes)
description: Crispy Belarusian grated potato pancakes served with sour cream.

steps.text: Finely grate potatoes and onion. Squeeze out as much liquid as possible through a cloth.
Mix with egg, flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Spoon tablespoons of mixture into the pan and flatten slightly. Fry 3–4 minutes per side until deeply golden and crispy.
Drain on paper towels. Serve immediately with cold sour cream.

name: Mtsvadi (Georgian Grilled Pork Skewers)
description: Cubes of pork marinated simply with onion and salt, then grilled over open coals — Georgia's everyday answer to a barbecue, cooked at home whenever there's a reason to gather.

steps.text: Cut the pork into large, even cubes.
Slice one onion into rings and grate the other.
Mix the pork with the grated onion, oil, salt, and pepper, and marinate for at least 1 hour, ideally longer.
Thread the pork onto skewers, alternating with the onion rings.
Grill over hot coals or a very hot grill pan, turning regularly, for 15-18 minutes until cooked through and charred at the edges.
Serve hot off the skewer, drizzled with pomegranate molasses if using, with fresh bread.

name: Salmon in Cream Sauce
description: Pan-seared salmon fillet in a rich cream, spinach, and white wine sauce.

steps.text: Season salmon with salt. Sear skin-side down in butter for 4 minutes until skin is crispy. Flip, cook 2 more minutes. Remove.
In the same pan, sauté minced shallot and garlic until soft.
Add white wine and reduce by half.
Add cream and simmer until slightly thickened. Add spinach and let it wilt.
Return salmon to the sauce. Heat through for 1–2 minutes. Finish with fresh dill and serve.

name: Mushroom Risotto
description: Slow-stirred Arborio rice with earthy mushrooms, white wine, and parmesan.

steps.text: Heat vegetable stock in a separate saucepan and keep it warm throughout cooking.
Sauté chopped onion in butter until soft and translucent. Add sliced mushrooms and cook until golden.
Add Arborio rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains turn translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine and stir until absorbed.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next.
After about 18–20 minutes, rice should be creamy and al dente. Remove from heat.
Stir in cold butter and grated parmesan (mantecatura). Season, rest 2 minutes, serve.

name: Döner Kebab
description: Shaved seasoned meat in flatbread with salad, tomato, onion, and garlic sauce.

steps.text: Slice the lamb or chicken thinly and season with salt and a little sumac.
Cook the meat on a very hot grill pan or under a broiler in thin layers, turning frequently until browned and lightly charred.
Warm the flatbread on a dry pan or briefly under the broiler.
Slice the tomato and onion and finely shred the cabbage.
Fill the flatbread with meat, cabbage, tomato, onion, garlic sauce, and red pepper sauce. Wrap and serve.

name: Shopska Salad
description: Bulgarian national salad with tomato, cucumber, peppers, and a blizzard of grated white cheese.

steps.text: Dice tomatoes, cucumber, and green pepper into chunky pieces.
Slice red onion very thin. Combine with vegetables.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt. Toss lightly.
Transfer to individual plates. Grate a thick layer of Bulgarian white cheese (sirene) over the top.
Garnish with fresh parsley. Do not mix after adding cheese — serve immediately.

name: Sarma (Balkan Stuffed Cabbage)
description: Tangy fermented cabbage rolls filled with pork, beef, and rice, braised for hours.

steps.text: Mix pork and beef mince with raw rice, sautéed onion, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Separate sauerkraut leaves. Place a tablespoon of filling on each leaf and roll tightly.
Layer smoked ribs on the bottom of a large pot. Pack rolls tightly on top.
Add a few whole peppercorns, bay leaves, and just enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to lowest heat. Cover and cook for 2–2.5 hours.
Sarma is always better the next day. Serve with sour cream and mashed potatoes.

name: Ramen
description: Rich Japanese noodle soup with tender pork belly, soft egg, and nori.

steps.text: Heat the prepared pork broth in a saucepan and keep it at a gentle simmer.
Cook the pork belly until browned and tender, then slice it thinly.
Soft-boil the eggs for about 7 minutes, cool in ice water, peel, and halve.
Cook the ramen noodles according to the package instructions and divide them between bowls.
Ladle the hot pork broth over the noodles.
Top with pork belly, soft-boiled egg, nori, bamboo shoots, and sliced green onion. Serve immediately.

name: Briam (Greek Roasted Vegetable Medley)
description: Zucchini, potato, and tomato slow-roasted together in olive oil — a simple, everyday Greek vegetable bake eaten warm or cold.

steps.text: Slice the zucchini, potatoes, tomatoes, and onion into rounds. Mince the garlic.
Arrange the vegetables in a baking dish, tucking in the garlic between layers.
Drizzle generously with olive oil, sprinkle with oregano and salt, and toss gently to coat.
Cover with foil and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for another 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized at the edges.
Scatter with parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Samsa (Central Asian Pastry)
description: Flaky oven-baked pastry triangles stuffed with spiced lamb and onion.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Finely dice the onion and mix with the lamb, cumin, salt and pepper.
Roll out the pastry and cut into 6 equal squares. Divide the filling between them.
Fold into triangles and press the edges firmly to seal. Place on a lined baking tray.
Brush with the measured egg wash and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Bake for 25–30 minutes, until golden and the filling is cooked through. Serve 2 pastries per portion.

name: Fakes (Greek Lentil Soup)
description: Simple lentil soup simmered with onion, garlic, and tomato, finished with olive oil and vinegar — a Greek weeknight classic all year round.

steps.text: Rinse the lentils and pick out any debris.
Dice the onion and carrot, and mince the garlic.
Heat olive oil in a pot and sauté the onion, carrot, and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add the lentils, canned tomatoes, bay leaf, and 900ml water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Season with salt and vinegar, and serve hot drizzled with extra olive oil.

name: Grilled Cheese Sandwich
description: Buttered bread, melted cheddar, crisped in a pan — the everyday American lunch that needs no recipe.

steps.text: Butter one side of each slice of bread.
Layer cheddar between two slices, buttered sides facing out.
Toast in a pan over medium heat, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Slice in half and serve immediately.

name: Wiener Schnitzel
description: Authentic Viennese veal schnitzel pounded thin and fried to a lacy golden crust.

steps.text: Pound veal between two sheets of plastic wrap to 3–4 mm thickness.
Season with salt and pepper. Bread using the standard 3-plate method: flour, egg, breadcrumbs.
Do not press the breadcrumbs — a loose coating creates the characteristic soufflé-like texture.
Heat a generous amount of clarified butter in a large pan. The schnitzel must swim in fat.
Fry for 2–3 minutes per side, continuously shaking the pan so fat flows over the top.
Drain on paper towels immediately. Serve with lemon, lingonberries, and parsley potatoes.

name: Seared Scallops
description: Golden butter-seared scallops with lemon, garlic, and thyme — elegant and quick.

steps.text: Pat scallops completely dry with paper towels — this is essential for a good sear.
Season with salt and pepper just before cooking.
Heat a pan over very high heat until nearly smoking. Add a mix of oil and butter.
Place scallops in the pan without moving. Sear for exactly 90 seconds until a deep golden crust forms.
Flip once. Add garlic and thyme. Baste with butter for 60 seconds. Squeeze lemon over and serve immediately.

name: Byrek (Albanian Filo Pie)
description: Flaky filo pastry pie filled with spinach and white cheese — Albanian street food staple.

steps.text: Wilt spinach in a hot pan. Squeeze out all moisture and chop roughly.
Mix spinach with crumbled white cheese, eggs, and olive oil. Season with salt.
Oil a round baking tin. Layer 3 filo sheets, brushing each with oil.
Spread spinach filling evenly. Layer 3 more oiled filo sheets on top.
Score the top and drizzle with oil. Bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until deep golden.
Splash with a little cold water when it comes out of the oven for extra crispness.

name: Paella
description: Spanish saffron rice with seafood, chicken, and chorizo cooked in a wide pan.

steps.text: Steep saffron in warm stock for 10 minutes.
In a wide paella pan, fry chicken and chorizo until golden. Remove and set aside.
Fry onion, pepper, and garlic in the same pan. Add tomato and smoked paprika.
Add rice and stir to coat in the oil. Pour in saffron stock. Do not stir again.
Return chicken and chorizo. Arrange shrimp and mussels on top. Cook on medium-low.
Cook 18–20 minutes until stock is absorbed and the bottom forms a crust (socarrat). Serve with lemon.

name: Chocolate Fondant
description: Warm dark chocolate cake with a molten flowing centre, served with vanilla ice cream.

steps.text: Melt dark chocolate and butter together in a bain-marie. Stir until smooth.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale and thick.
Fold chocolate mixture into eggs. Sift in flour and fold gently.
Butter and cocoa-dust ramekins. Pour in batter to ¾ full. Refrigerate up to 24 hours at this stage.
Bake at 200°C for exactly 10–12 minutes — edges firm, centre still liquid.
Rest 30 seconds. Run a knife around edge and invert onto plate. Serve immediately with ice cream.

name: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, finished with feta and herbs.

steps.text: Dice the onion and pepper. Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the vegetables for 7 minutes.
Add chopped garlic, cumin, paprika and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 10 minutes.
Make 4 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each one. Cover and cook for 5–7 minutes, until the whites are set; cook longer for firm yolks.
Crumble over the feta and chopped parsley. Divide into 2 portions. Extra bread is optional and is not included in the quantities.

name: Beef Tacos
description: Corn tortillas filled with spiced ground beef, salsa, avocado, and cheese.

steps.text: Brown ground beef in a pan over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks.
Drain excess fat. Add taco seasoning and a splash of water. Simmer 3–4 minutes.
Warm corn tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side.
Mash avocado with lime juice and salt for quick guacamole.
Fill tortillas with beef, salsa, guacamole, cheese, and sour cream. Serve immediately.

name: Gyoza
description: Pan-fried Japanese dumplings with a crispy bottom and juicy pork-cabbage filling.

steps.text: Salt shredded cabbage, let stand 5 minutes, then squeeze out all moisture.
Mix pork mince with cabbage, minced garlic, grated ginger, sesame oil, soy sauce, and white pepper.
Place a teaspoon of filling in the centre of each wrapper. Fold and pleat the edges to seal.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high. Place gyoza flat-side down and cook until golden on the bottom.
Add a splash of water and cover immediately. Steam for 3–4 minutes until wrappers are translucent.
Uncover and cook off remaining water. Serve with soy-vinegar dipping sauce.

name: Zwiebelkuchen (German Onion Cake)
description: Savoury German onion tart with bacon, eggs, and cream on a yeast pastry base.

steps.text: Cover the prepared dough and leave to rise for about 1 hour, or follow its packet instructions.
Meanwhile, thinly slice the onions. Melt the butter in a pan and soften the onions for 20–25 minutes. Cook the diced bacon with them and let the mixture cool slightly.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Roll out the dough to line a 20 × 25 cm baking tray.
Whisk the eggs, sour cream, salt and caraway seeds. Stir in the cooled onion and bacon mixture and spread over the dough.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the filling is set and the base is cooked. Cut into 6 portions.

name: Apple Strudel
description: Austrian flaky pastry filled with spiced apple, raisins, and cinnamon sugar.

steps.text: Peel and thinly slice apples. Mix with sugar, cinnamon, raisins, and chopped walnuts.
Fry breadcrumbs in butter until golden. Cool.
Lay out a damp cloth. Layer 3–4 filo sheets, brushing each with melted butter.
Scatter breadcrumbs on the pastry, leaving a border. Place apple filling along one edge.
Use the cloth to roll strudel tightly like a log. Transfer to a baking tray seam-side down.
Brush with butter and bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until golden. Dust with icing sugar.

name: Zrazy (Eastern European Beef Rolls)
description: Thin beef slices rolled around hard-boiled egg, pickles, and mustard, braised in gravy.

steps.text: Pound thin beef slices between cling film. Spread with mustard and season.
Place a slice of pickled cucumber and quartered hard-boiled egg on each slice. Roll tightly and secure with a toothpick.
Dust with flour and brown on all sides in hot oil.
Add sliced onion to the pan and sauté briefly.
Pour in beef stock. Cover and braise on low heat for 35–40 minutes.
Remove toothpicks. Serve in the braising sauce with mashed potatoes or kasha.

name: Pasta al Pomodoro
description: The simplest Italian weeknight pasta — tomatoes, garlic, basil, and olive oil, on the table in twenty minutes.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a pan and gently fry the garlic until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the canned tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Season with salt and tear in most of the basil leaves.
Drain the pasta and toss it through the sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Serve topped with grated parmesan and the remaining basil.

name: Napoleon Cake
description: Iconic Russian layered mille-feuille with hundreds of pastry sheets and custard cream.

steps.text: Make custard: heat milk with vanilla. Whisk eggs and sugar, add flour, then pour warm milk in slowly. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until thick. Cool completely, then beat in cold butter.
Roll puff pastry paper-thin and cut into 6–8 equal rectangles. Bake each at 200°C for 10–12 minutes until golden and crispy.
Layer pastry sheets and custard cream alternately, pressing each layer down gently.
Crumble the least attractive pastry sheet into fine crumbs.
Coat the top and sides of the cake with the crumbs. Refrigerate overnight — the pastry must absorb the cream.

name: Brudet (Croatian Fish Stew)
description: Dalmatian-style tomato and white fish stew served over buttery polenta.

components.name: water
components.comment: for polenta; adjust to packet instructions

components.name: salt
components.comment: 2 g for stew; 2 g for polenta

steps.text: Dice the onion. Heat the olive oil in a wide pot and cook the onion for 8 minutes. Add chopped garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the canned tomatoes, vinegar, 2 g salt and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Cut the fish into large pieces and add to the sauce. Cover and simmer gently for 10–15 minutes, until cooked through; shake the pot instead of stirring vigorously.
Meanwhile, bring the water and remaining 2 g salt to a boil. Whisk in the polenta and cook according to its packet instructions, adding water if necessary. Stir in the butter.
Divide the polenta and fish stew into 4 portions and scatter with parsley.

name: Pumpkin Cream Soup
description: Velvety pumpkin soup with ginger, coconut milk, and a swirl of cream.

steps.text: Peel and cube squash. Chop onion and garlic.
Sauté onion in oil until soft. Add garlic and grated ginger, cook 1 minute.
Add squash and vegetable stock. Bring to boil and simmer 20 minutes until squash is tender.
Add coconut milk and blend until completely smooth.
Season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. Serve with a swirl of cream and toasted seeds.

name: Knödel with Gravy
description: Bavarian bread dumplings with herb stuffing, served in a rich roast gravy.

steps.text: Slice stale bread into cubes. Pour warm milk over and let soak for 15–20 minutes.
Sauté diced onion in butter until golden. Add to bread with eggs, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Mix thoroughly. If too wet, add a spoonful of flour.
With wet hands, form into firm round dumplings.
Simmer gently (not boiling) in salted water for 20 minutes. Turn once halfway.
Serve with roast gravy and braised red cabbage.

name: Poke Bowl
description: Hawaiian-style bowl of sushi rice topped with fresh salmon, avocado, and sesame.

steps.text: Cook and season sushi rice with rice vinegar. Let cool to room temperature.
Cube fresh sashimi-grade salmon. Marinate briefly in soy sauce and sesame oil.
Slice avocado and cucumber. Prepare any other toppings.
Place rice in a bowl. Arrange salmon, avocado, cucumber, and edamame in sections on top.
Drizzle with soy sauce and sesame oil. Sprinkle sesame seeds and serve.

name: Caesar Salad with Chicken
description: Crisp romaine, grilled chicken, parmesan shavings, and croutons in Caesar dressing.

steps.text: Season chicken breast with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Grill or pan-fry for 5–6 minutes per side. Rest and slice.
Make dressing: blend anchovies, garlic, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, parmesan, and mayo until smooth.
Tear romaine into large pieces and toss with just enough dressing to coat.
Add croutons, shaved parmesan, and sliced chicken on top. Serve immediately.

name: Spaghetti Carbonara
description: Creamy Roman pasta with crispy pancetta, eggs, and pecorino — no cream needed.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook spaghetti until al dente.
Fry pancetta in a dry pan over medium heat until crispy, then remove from heat.
Whisk together eggs and finely grated pecorino in a bowl. Add plenty of black pepper.
Reserve a cup of pasta cooking water, then drain the pasta.
Add hot pasta to the pancetta pan off the heat. Pour egg mixture over and toss quickly.
Add splashes of pasta water to loosen the sauce to a creamy consistency. Serve immediately.

name: Pirog (Russian Filled Pie)
description: Large baked Russian pie filled with cabbage and egg or salmon — perfect for gatherings.

steps.text: Make yeasted dough and let rise 1 hour.
Finely shred cabbage and sauté with onion in butter until soft. Season with salt and dill.
Chop hard-boiled eggs and stir into the cooled cabbage filling.
Divide dough in half. Roll one half into a rectangle and place on a baking tray.
Spread filling in the centre. Roll second half of dough and place on top, sealing all edges.
Brush with egg wash. Poke steam holes. Bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until golden. Rest 15 minutes.

name: Gulaschsuppe (German Goulash Soup)
description: Spicy, paprika-rich German beef soup with peppers, potatoes, and caraway.

steps.text: Cut the beef into small cubes. Heat the oil in a pot and brown the beef in batches, about 10 minutes in total. Remove to a plate.
Dice the onion and pepper and cook them in the same pot for 5 minutes. Take the pot off the heat and stir in both paprikas.
Return the beef and add the tomato paste, caraway seeds and beef stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer for 45 minutes, then add diced potatoes.
Cook for another 20 minutes, or until the beef and potatoes are tender. Add water if required to keep a soup consistency.
Stir in the measured salt and pepper and divide into 4 portions. Extra bread or sour cream is optional and is not included in the quantities.

name: Egg Fried Rice
description: Quick wok-tossed rice with scrambled eggs, soy sauce, and sesame oil.

steps.text: Use day-old cold rice for best results — fresh rice is too wet.
Heat wok over very high heat until smoking. Add oil and minced garlic, stir for 30 seconds.
Add rice and press it against the hot wok surface. Toss every 30 seconds.
Push rice to the side, crack eggs in and scramble them. Mix into the rice.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil, toss well. Scatter sliced green onion and serve.

name: Sup s Frikadelkami (Russian Meatball Soup)
description: Light broth with small meatballs, potato, and carrot — a quick, everyday soup Russian and Ukrainian families make for a fast lunch.

steps.text: Grate half the onion finely and mix it into the beef mince along with the egg, rice, salt, and pepper.
Shape the mixture into small meatballs, about the size of a walnut.
Bring 1.2 liters of water to a boil in a pot.
Dice the remaining onion, potatoes, and carrot, and add them to the pot along with the bay leaf.
Simmer for 10 minutes, then gently drop in the meatballs.
Simmer for another 12-15 minutes until the meatballs and vegetables are cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the dill, and serve hot.

name: Cherry Varenyky
description: Sweet Ukrainian dumplings filled with sour cherries, dusted with sugar and cream.

steps.text: Make dough: combine flour, egg, a pinch of salt, and warm water. Knead until smooth and elastic. Rest 30 minutes.
Pit sour cherries. Toss with sugar and let sit 10 minutes — this draws out some juice.
Roll dough thin and cut circles with a glass. Place 3–4 cherries on each circle.
Pinch edges tightly to seal — cherry juice can cause them to open if not sealed well.
Boil in salted water for 5 minutes after they float. Serve with sour cream and a dusting of sugar.

name: Fasolada (Greek White Bean Soup)
description: Rustic white bean soup simmered with tomato, carrot, and olive oil — considered Greece's national comfort dish, eaten in homes through the cold months.

steps.text: If using dried beans, ensure they've been soaked overnight and drained; canned beans can be rinsed and used directly.
Dice the carrot, celery, and onion.
Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a pot and sauté the onion, carrot, and celery for 5 minutes.
Add the beans, canned tomatoes, bay leaf, and enough water to cover generously.
Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, until the beans are tender and the soup has thickened slightly.
Season with salt, stir in the remaining olive oil, and serve hot with bread.

name: Buckwheat Kasha with Mushrooms
description: Nutty roasted buckwheat cooked with dried mushrooms and caramelised onion.

steps.text: Soak dried mushrooms in warm water for 20 minutes. Drain, reserving the liquid. Chop mushrooms.
Toast buckwheat in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes until aromatic.
Add mushroom soaking liquid and water (2 parts liquid to 1 part buckwheat). Bring to boil.
Add mushrooms, reduce heat, cover, and cook 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, caramelise diced onion in oil with garlic.
Fluff buckwheat, stir in caramelised onion. Season with salt and pepper.

name: Rührei mit Speck (Scrambled Eggs with Bacon)
description: Soft scrambled eggs with crisp bacon, eaten with bread — a common simple German breakfast or light dinner.

steps.text: Fry the bacon in a pan until crisp, then remove and set aside, leaving the fat in the pan.
Whisk the eggs with milk, salt, and pepper.
Melt the butter in the same pan over low heat and pour in the eggs.
Stir gently and continuously over low heat until softly set, about 3 minutes.
Fold in the bacon, scatter with chives, and serve with bread.

name: Tandoori Chicken
description: Chicken marinated in yogurt and spices, roasted in a scorching oven until charred.

steps.text: Mix the yogurt, lemon juice, tandoori masala, crushed garlic, grated ginger, oil and salt.
Coat the chicken with the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 4 hours.
Preheat the oven to 220°C. Arrange the chicken on a lined tray and roast for 20–25 minutes, until cooked through.
Brush with the melted butter during the final 5 minutes. Divide into 2 portions. Extra rice, bread or chutney is optional and is not included in the quantities.

name: Blueberry Muffins
description: Bakery-style muffins bursting with fresh blueberries and a crunchy sugar top.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 190°C. Line a muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix dry ingredients: flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, lemon zest.
Mix wet: eggs, buttermilk, melted butter, vanilla.
Fold wet into dry until just combined — a few lumps are fine. Do not over-mix.
Fold in blueberries gently. Fill cases to the brim. Sprinkle demerara sugar on top.
Bake for 20–22 minutes until tops are domed and a skewer comes out clean.

name: Spatzle with Butter
description: Soft Swabian egg noodle dumplings tossed in browned butter and fresh chives.

steps.text: Mix flour, eggs, milk, nutmeg, and salt into a thick, sticky batter. Beat until it pulls into strings.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Press batter through a spätzle press or colander with large holes directly into boiling water.
Boil until they float, then 1 more minute. Remove with a slotted spoon.
In a pan, heat butter until it foams and turns golden brown. Toss spätzle in the browned butter.
Season with salt and scatter fresh chives. Serve as a side or main.

name: Shawarma
description: Spiced chicken wraps with vegetables, pickles and yogurt-garlic sauce.

components.name: olive oil
components.comment: 10 ml for marinade; 5 ml for sauce

components.name: lemon juice
components.comment: 15 ml for marinade; 15 ml for sauce

components.name: salt
components.comment: 1 g for marinade; 1 g for sauce

steps.text: Coat the chicken with the shawarma spice, 15 ml lemon juice, 10 ml olive oil and 1 g salt. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour.
Mix the yogurt with crushed garlic, the remaining lemon juice, olive oil and salt to make the sauce. Keep refrigerated.
Cook the chicken in a hot pan or on a grill for 10–15 minutes, turning as needed, until cooked through. Rest briefly, then slice.
Thinly slice the onion, tomato and pickles. Toss the onion with sumac.
Warm the flatbreads. Divide the chicken, vegetables and sauce between them and roll up. Makes 2 wraps.

name: Gemista (Greek Stuffed Tomatoes and Peppers)
description: Tomatoes and peppers hollowed out and baked with a herby rice filling — a summer staple Greek families cook whenever the garden gives too many tomatoes.

components.name: potatoes
components.comment: cut into wedges, to bake alongside

steps.text: Slice the tops off the tomatoes and peppers and scoop out the insides, reserving the tomato pulp and keeping the tops.
Finely dice the onion and chop the reserved tomato pulp.
Mix the rice, onion, tomato pulp, parsley, mint, half the olive oil, and salt to make the filling.
Fill each hollowed vegetable about two-thirds full with the rice mixture, to leave room for the rice to expand, and replace the tops.
Arrange in a baking dish with the potato wedges tucked around them, drizzle with the remaining oil, and add a splash of water to the dish.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 55-60 minutes until the vegetables are soft and the rice is fully cooked.
Let rest for 10 minutes before serving warm or at room temperature.

name: Lentil Soup (Linsensuppe)
description: Hearty German lentil soup with smoked sausage, carrot, and celery.

steps.text: Dice the onion, carrot and celery. Heat the oil in a pot and cook the vegetables for 8 minutes. Add the bay leaf and thyme.
Rinse the dry lentils and add them with the sliced sausage and vegetable stock. Bring to a boil.
Simmer for 30–35 minutes, until the lentils are tender. Remove the bay leaf.
Mash a ladleful of lentils and return them to the pot to thicken the soup.
Stir in the vinegar, measured salt and pepper. Add a little water if needed and divide into 4 portions.

name: Pan con Tomate
description: Toasted bread rubbed with garlic and ripe tomato, finished with olive oil — the simplest everyday Spanish snack.

steps.text: Slice the bread and toast until golden and crisp.
Cut the garlic clove in half and rub it over one side of the toasted bread.
Halve the tomatoes and grate the cut side directly onto the bread, discarding the skin, or rub the halves over the bread until it's coated in pulp.
Drizzle generously with olive oil, sprinkle with salt, and serve immediately.

name: Focaccia
description: Fluffy Italian flatbread dimpled with olive oil, sea salt, and rosemary.

steps.text: Mix flour, yeast, salt, and water. Add olive oil and knead for 8 minutes. Place in an oiled bowl.
Stretch and fold the dough 4 times over 2 hours. Refrigerate overnight for best flavour.
Transfer to an oiled baking tray. Stretch gently to fill the tray. Rest 45 minutes.
Dimple all over deeply with your fingers. Drizzle very generously with olive oil.
Top with rosemary sprigs, sliced garlic, and flaky sea salt.
Bake at 230°C for 20–22 minutes until golden. Eat warm.

name: Burek
description: Flaky filo pastry coils filled with minced meat or cheese — Balkan street food staple.

steps.text: Make filling: brown beef mince with diced onion, season with salt and pepper. Cool.
Brush each filo sheet with oil. Spread a thin layer of meat filling along one edge.
Roll into a long thin log. Coil the log into a spiral in a greased round baking tin.
Repeat with remaining filo and filling, continuing the coil.
Brush top with oil or egg wash. Bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until deep golden brown.
Remove from oven and splash with cold water — this makes the pastry crispier. Rest 10 minutes. Serve with yogurt.

name: Pelmeni
description: Russian bite-sized dumplings filled with pork and beef mince, boiled and served with butter.

steps.text: Make stiff dough from flour, egg, water, and salt. Knead and rest 30 minutes.
Mix minced pork and beef with finely grated onion, salt, and black pepper.
Roll dough thin and cut rounds. Fill each with a small ball of meat.
Fold into a half-moon, seal edges, then bring the two corners together and pinch to form the classic shape.
Boil in salted water for 7–8 minutes after they float.
Toss with butter. Serve with sour cream and a splash of vinegar, or in the cooking broth.

name: Börek Pita (Serbian Cheese Pie)
description: Flaky baked filo pie with a rich white cheese and egg filling — Serbian comfort food.

steps.text: Mix crumbled white cheese with eggs and sour cream. Season lightly (cheese is already salty).
Layer 2–3 oiled filo sheets in a baking tray. Spread cheese mixture over them.
Layer another 2–3 sheets on top, brushing each with oil.
Score the top layer into squares or diamonds. Drizzle with oil.
Bake at 190°C for 30–35 minutes until golden and flaky.
Let cool slightly. Traditionally splashed with cold water for extra flakiness.

name: Lasagna
description: Layered pasta bake with rich Bolognese, creamy béchamel, and parmesan crust.

steps.text: Make the meat sauce: brown the beef mince with chopped onion and carrot. Add the tomatoes and simmer for about 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and have the prepared béchamel ready.
Spread a thin layer of meat sauce on the bottom of the baking dish.
Layer lasagna sheets, meat sauce, and béchamel. Repeat until the ingredients are used.
Finish with béchamel and grated parmesan.
Bake covered with foil for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake for another 20 minutes until golden. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

name: Satsivi (Chicken in Walnut Sauce)
description: Poached chicken served cold, blanketed in a thick, spiced walnut sauce — a centerpiece dish at Georgian holiday tables and family celebrations.

steps.text: Poach the chicken in salted water with half the onion until cooked through, about 25 minutes. Reserve the broth.
Let the chicken cool slightly, then remove the skin if desired and set the meat aside.
Finely grind the walnuts, remaining onion, and garlic into a smooth paste, using a splash of reserved broth to loosen if needed.
Warm the walnut paste in a pan with the chicken stock, whisking until smooth.
Stir in vinegar, khmeli-suneli, turmeric, and salt, and simmer gently for 10 minutes to thicken slightly.
Pour the sauce over the chicken pieces, coating well, and chill for at least an hour before serving.

name: PB&J Sandwich
description: Peanut butter and jelly on soft bread — the quintessential no-cook American lunch, especially for kids.

steps.text: Spread peanut butter generously on two slices of bread.
Spread jam on the other two slices.
Press the slices together, peanut butter to jam, and slice diagonally to serve.

name: Potato Varenyky
description: Ukrainian dumplings stuffed with mashed potato and caramelised onion, served with sour cream.

steps.text: Make dough: combine flour, egg, water, and salt. Knead 5–7 minutes until smooth. Rest 30 minutes covered.
Boil potatoes until tender. Mash with butter and salt.
Caramelise diced onion in butter until golden. Mix half into mashed potato for the filling.
Roll dough thin. Cut circles with a glass. Place a teaspoon of filling in each.
Fold and pinch edges tightly to seal. Boil in salted water for 4–5 minutes after they float.
Toss with remaining caramelised onion. Serve with sour cream and fresh dill.

name: Ukha (Fish Soup)
description: Clear Eastern European fish broth with potato, carrot, and fresh dill.

steps.text: Place fish pieces in a pot of cold water with onion, parsley root, bay leaf, and peppercorns. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer gently for 20–25 minutes. Remove fish and strain the broth.
Add diced potato and carrot to the clear broth. Simmer until tender.
Return fish pieces. Season with salt.
Serve with a generous handful of fresh dill and a splash of vodka (optional, traditional).

name: Omelette Nature
description: Plain French omelette, folded soft and buttery — the everyday quick dinner or breakfast in most French homes.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper until just combined.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over medium heat until foaming.
Pour in the eggs and let them set slightly at the edges, then gently push them toward the center with a spatula.
Once mostly set but still soft in the middle, fold the omelette in half or thirds.
Slide onto a plate and serve immediately.

name: Vegetarian Borscht
description: Vibrant Eastern European beetroot soup with cabbage, potato, and sour cream.

steps.text: Grate the beetroot and carrot and dice the onion. Heat the oil in a pan and cook the vegetables for 10 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and vinegar.
Bring the vegetable stock to a boil in a pot. Add diced potatoes and shredded cabbage and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the beetroot mixture and simmer for another 10 minutes, until all the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the measured sugar, salt and pepper. Divide into 4 bowls and serve each with 20 g sour cream and chopped dill.

name: Tzatziki (Greek Yogurt and Cucumber Dip)
description: Thick strained yogurt with grated cucumber, garlic, and olive oil — a fixture on Greek tables, spooned onto almost anything.

steps.text: Grate the cucumber and squeeze out as much liquid as possible using a clean kitchen towel.
Mince the garlic finely.
Combine the yogurt, cucumber, garlic, olive oil, vinegar, dill, and salt in a bowl.
Stir well and chill for at least 15 minutes before serving with bread or grilled meat.

name: Sogan Dolma (Turkish Stuffed Onion)
description: Tender whole onions stuffed with spiced rice and pine nuts, braised in tomato.

steps.text: Peel onions. Boil whole in water for 10–12 minutes until outer layers soften.
Cool and carefully separate the outer layers to use as wraps. Reserve inner parts, chop and sauté.
Mix sautéed onion with rice, pine nuts, currants, cinnamon, allspice, salt, and a little oil.
Place filling inside each onion layer and roll up. Pack tightly in a pot.
Mix tomato paste with water and lemon juice. Pour over dolma.
Simmer covered for 35–40 minutes until rice is cooked. Serve at room temperature.

name: Pepperoni Pizza
description: Golden pizza loaded with spicy pepperoni and stretchy melted mozzarella.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 250°C with baking tray inside.
Roll or stretch dough into a round. Spread tomato sauce evenly.
Cover with shredded mozzarella, then layer pepperoni slices on top.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until cheese is bubbling and crust is golden.
Let cool for 2 minutes before slicing and serving.

name: Nachos
description: Tortilla chips loaded with melted cheese, jalapeños, sour cream, and salsa.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Spread 150 g tortilla chips in a single layer on a baking tray.
Grate the cheddar and Monterey Jack and scatter both evenly over the chips.
Add the sliced jalapeños and bake for 8–10 minutes, until the cheese has melted.
Divide into 3 portions and serve immediately with the measured salsa, sour cream and guacamole.

name: Bouillabaisse
description: Provençal fisherman's stew with saffron, fennel, and a variety of fresh seafood.

steps.text: Sauté fennel, onion, and garlic in olive oil until soft. Add saffron.
Add crushed tomatoes, fish stock, orange zest, and a pinch of cayenne. Simmer 20 minutes.
Add firm fish pieces first. Cook 5 minutes. Add softer fish, then shellfish.
Cover and cook until mussels open and all seafood is cooked — about 5–8 minutes more.
Season with salt. Serve with rouille (garlic-saffron mayo) on toasted baguette slices.

name: Waffles with Berries
description: Crispy Belgian waffles served with fresh berries and whipped cream.

steps.text: Separate eggs. Whisk yolks with sugar, vanilla, melted butter, and milk.
Sift flour and baking powder into the mixture. Combine.
Whip egg whites to stiff peaks. Fold gently into batter — this makes them extra light.
Heat waffle iron and grease lightly. Pour in batter and cook until golden and crispy.
Serve with fresh berries and freshly whipped cream. Dust with icing sugar.

name: Flammkuchen (Tarte Flambée)
description: Thin Alsatian flatbread topped with crème fraîche, bacon, and onion.

steps.text: Preheat oven to maximum temperature (250°C+) with baking stone or tray inside.
Roll dough extremely thin — almost cracker-thin.
Spread a thin layer of crème fraîche seasoned with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Scatter thinly sliced onion and bacon lardons over the top.
Bake for 8–10 minutes until edges are charred and topping is bubbling. Slice and serve immediately.

name: Croque Monsieur
description: French toasted ham and cheese sandwich with béchamel sauce and golden crust.

steps.text: Make a small béchamel: melt butter, stir in flour, then add warm milk gradually. Season with nutmeg and salt.
Spread Dijon mustard on one slice of bread. Add ham and grated Gruyère. Top with second slice.
Spread béchamel on top of the sandwich. Sprinkle with more Gruyère.
Bake or grill until cheese is bubbling and deep golden. Serve hot.

name: Čorba (Balkan Lamb Soup)
description: Rich Balkan lamb and vegetable soup thickened with egg and vinegar.

steps.text: Cut lamb into pieces. Cover with cold water, bring to boil, skim foam, then simmer 45 minutes.
Add diced potato, carrot, and celery. Simmer 20 more minutes.
Remove a cup of hot broth. Whisk with egg and vinegar to make the thickener.
Reduce heat to very low. Slowly stir the egg mixture into the soup — do not boil after this step or it will curdle.
Season with salt, paprika, and chopped parsley. The soup should have a mild sourness.

name: Revithia (Greek Chickpea Soup)
description: Slow-simmered chickpeas with onion, olive oil, and lemon — a simple Sunday soup eaten in Greek homes for generations, especially on the islands.

steps.text: If using dried chickpeas, ensure they've been soaked overnight; canned chickpeas can be drained and rinsed and used directly.
Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a pot and cook the onion and garlic until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the chickpeas, bay leaf, and enough water to cover generously.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 minutes until the chickpeas are tender and the soup has thickened slightly.
Remove the bay leaf, season with salt and lemon juice, and stir in the remaining olive oil before serving.

name: Pasta Bolognese
description: Slow-simmered meat ragù with vegetables and tomatoes over al dente spaghetti.

steps.text: Dice the onion, carrot and celery. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan and soften the vegetables for 8 minutes.
Add the beef mince and cook for 5 minutes, breaking it up. Add the wine and simmer for 2–3 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, milk, salt and pepper. Simmer gently for 30–40 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding a little water if needed.
Cook the spaghetti according to its packet instructions. Drain, reserving a little cooking water.
Toss the spaghetti with the sauce, loosening with reserved water if needed. Divide into 3 portions and top with the grated Parmesan.

name: Khachapuri (Adjarian Cheese Bread)
description: Boat-shaped bread filled with molten cheese, butter, and a raw egg cracked on top — Georgia's most iconic everyday food, eaten at breakfast, lunch, or as a shared centerpiece.

components.name: farmer's cheese
components.comment: or a mix of mozzarella and feta

steps.text: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in warm milk and let it stand for 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour and salt, then work in the yeast mixture to form a soft dough. Knead for 8 minutes.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled.
Divide the dough in two and roll each piece into an oval. Fold the long edges inward and twist the ends to form a boat shape.
Fill each boat generously with cheese and place on a baking tray.
Bake at 220°C (425°F) for 12-15 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling.
Remove from the oven, crack an egg into the center of each boat, and return to the oven for 2 minutes until the egg is just set.
Top with a pat of butter and serve immediately, mixing the egg and cheese together before tearing off bread to dip.

name: Enchiladas
description: Rolled corn tortillas filled with chicken and smothered in red chili sauce and cheese.

steps.text: Warm tortillas in a dry pan to make them pliable.
Dip each tortilla briefly in enchilada sauce. Fill with shredded chicken and diced onion.
Roll up and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour remaining enchilada sauce over the top. Sprinkle generously with cheese.
Bake at 190°C for 20–25 minutes until cheese is melted and edges are bubbling.
Serve with sour cream, guacamole, and fresh cilantro.

name: Pâtes au Beurre et Parmesan (Buttered Pasta with Parmesan)
description: The pasta French parents make when there's nothing else in the fridge — butter, parmesan, and a good pasta.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente.
Reserve a small cup of pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Return the pasta to the pot off the heat and add the butter, tossing until melted and glossy.
Add the grated parmesan and a splash of pasta water, tossing to form a light sauce.
Season with black pepper and serve immediately.

name: Beef Stroganoff
description: Tender strips of beef in a rich sour cream and mustard sauce, served over egg noodles.

steps.text: Slice beef into thin strips against the grain. Season with salt and pepper.
Sear beef in very hot butter in small batches — do not crowd the pan. Cook 60–90 seconds per batch. Remove and set aside.
In same pan, sauté onion until soft. Add sliced mushrooms and cook until golden.
Add mustard and a splash of beef stock. Reduce slightly.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in sour cream — do not boil or it will split.
Return beef to the sauce, heat through briefly. Serve over egg noodles with fresh parsley.

name: French Mushroom Omelette
description: Fluffy French-style omelette folded around sautéed mushrooms and melted cheese.

components.name: butter
components.comment: 10 g for mushrooms; 5 g for eggs

steps.text: Slice the mushrooms and cook in 10 g butter until golden and their moisture has evaporated. Set aside.
Whisk the 3 eggs with 0.5 g salt until uniform.
Melt the remaining 5 g butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour in the eggs.
Gently draw the set egg from the edges towards the centre while tilting the pan so the uncooked egg fills the gaps.
When the surface is almost set, add the mushrooms, grated vegetarian cheese and chopped chives to one half.
Fold the omelette in half and slide onto a plate. Serve immediately.

name: Chocolate Brownie
description: Dense fudgy chocolate squares with a crackly top and gooey centre.

steps.text: Melt butter and chocolate together. Stir until glossy and smooth. Cool slightly.
Whisk eggs and sugar until thick and the mixture holds a ribbon for 3 seconds.
Fold chocolate mixture into eggs. Sift in flour, cocoa, and salt. Fold until just combined.
Pour into a buttered lined tin. Bake at 180°C for 20–22 minutes.
Brownies are done when edges are set but centre still looks slightly underdone. They firm up as they cool.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting — this is the hardest part.

name: Pasta Primavera
description: Light spring pasta tossed with seasonal vegetables, garlic, and olive oil.

steps.text: Cook pasta in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve pasta water.
Slice zucchini and bell pepper. Sauté in olive oil over medium-high heat until slightly charred.
Add garlic, then cherry tomatoes. Cook until tomatoes burst slightly.
Add peas in the last 2 minutes.
Toss cooked pasta with vegetables, a splash of pasta water, olive oil, and grated Parmesan. Scatter fresh basil.

name: Horta Vrasta (Greek Boiled Greens with Lemon)
description: Simply boiled leafy greens dressed with olive oil and lemon — an everyday Greek side eaten with bread and feta.

steps.text: Wash the greens thoroughly, trimming any tough stems.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and add the greens.
Boil for 8-10 minutes until tender, then drain well.
Transfer to a serving dish while still warm.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice, and serve with bread.

name: Tortilla de Patatas
description: Classic Spanish potato and egg omelette, eaten warm or at room temperature — a household staple across Spain.

steps.text: Peel and thinly slice the potatoes and onion.
Heat the olive oil in a pan over medium-low heat and gently cook the potatoes and onion, stirring occasionally, until soft but not browned, about 15 minutes.
Drain the potatoes and onion, reserving the oil, and let them cool slightly.
Beat the eggs with salt in a large bowl, then fold in the potatoes and onion.
Heat a little of the reserved oil in a nonstick pan, pour in the mixture, and cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes.
Place a plate over the pan, flip the tortilla onto it, then slide it back into the pan to cook the other side for 3-4 minutes.
Slide onto a plate and let rest for a few minutes before slicing.

name: Crni Rižoto (Black Risotto)
description: Dramatic Croatian cuttlefish ink risotto with seafood and white wine.

steps.text: Clean cuttlefish and cut into rings. Reserve ink sacs if whole.
Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil. Add cuttlefish rings and cook 3 minutes.
Add rice, stir to coat. Pour in white wine and stir until absorbed.
Add squid ink and stir — the rice will turn dramatically black.
Add warm fish stock ladle by ladle, stirring constantly, for 18–20 minutes.
Season with salt. Finish with olive oil and fresh parsley. Serve with crusty bread.

name: Nalysnyky (Filled Crêpes)
description: Thin Ukrainian crêpes filled with sweetened cottage cheese and baked in cream.

steps.text: Make thin crêpe batter from flour, eggs, milk, and melted butter. Rest 15 minutes.
Fry thin crêpes in a lightly buttered pan.
Mix farmer's cheese with sugar, vanilla, and egg yolk for the filling.
Spread filling on each crêpe, fold into a rectangle or roll up.
Arrange in a buttered baking dish. Pour sour cream over.
Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes until tops are golden. Serve warm with jam.

name: Huevos a la Mexicana
description: Scrambled eggs cooked with tomato, onion, and chili — a fast, everyday Mexican breakfast eaten with tortillas.

steps.text: Finely dice the tomato, onion, and jalapeño.
Heat oil in a pan and cook the onion and jalapeño until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add the tomato and cook for another 3 minutes until it breaks down slightly.
Beat the eggs and pour into the pan, stirring gently until softly scrambled, about 3 minutes.
Season with salt and serve hot with warm corn tortillas.

name: Pancakes
description: Fluffy American-style buttermilk pancakes served with maple syrup and berries.

steps.text: Mix dry ingredients: flour, baking powder, baking soda, sugar, and salt.
Mix wet: buttermilk, eggs, and melted butter.
Combine wet and dry until just mixed — lumps are fine. Do not over-stir.
Let batter rest 5 minutes. Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat with a small knob of butter.
Pour a ladleful of batter. Cook until bubbles form on the surface and edges look set, about 2 minutes.
Flip once and cook 1 more minute. Serve with maple syrup and fresh berries.

name: Tarator (Balkan Cold Yogurt Soup)
description: Refreshing cold Balkan soup of yogurt, cucumber, garlic, dill, and walnuts.

steps.text: Finely grate cucumber and squeeze out excess liquid.
Mix yogurt with cold water to a soup-like consistency.
Add cucumber, crushed garlic, chopped walnuts, and fresh dill.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes. Serve in chilled bowls with ice cubes if desired.

name: Sahanda Yumurta (Turkish Fried Eggs)
description: Simple pan-fried eggs finished with a sizzling paprika butter — an everyday Turkish breakfast.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat.
Crack the eggs into the pan and cook until whites are set, about 3 minutes.
In a separate small pan, melt a little extra butter with paprika until it sizzles and turns red, about 30 seconds.
Season the eggs with salt, pour the paprika butter over the top, and serve immediately with bread.

name: Syrniki (Cottage Cheese Pancakes)
description: Pan-fried Ukrainian cottage cheese pancakes served warm with sour cream and jam.

steps.text: If cheese is wet, strain through a cheesecloth for 1 hour to remove excess moisture.
Mix cheese with eggs, sugar, vanilla, and enough flour to make a soft but manageable dough.
Dust hands with flour. Shape into small round patties about 1.5 cm thick.
Dust with flour. Pan-fry in oil over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side until golden.
Serve warm with sour cream and jam or honey.

name: Solyanka
description: Tangy Russian soup with mixed meats, olives, pickles, and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Dice the onion and cook in the oil for about 7 minutes, until softened. Add the tomato paste and cook for 3 minutes.
Slice the sausage, ham and drained pickles and add them to the pot.
Pour in the beef stock, add the olives and capers and bring to a simmer.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes. Stir in the lemon juice and pepper. Taste before adding any extra salt because the sausage, pickles and broth already contain salt.
Divide into 4 bowls and top each with 20 g sour cream.

name: Chicken Biryani
description: Fragrant basmati rice layered with spiced chicken, fried onion, and saffron.
