steps.text: Marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, and biryani spices for 2 hours.
Parboil basmati rice in salted water until about 70% cooked, then drain.
Cook marinated chicken in ghee until half done, about 15 minutes.
In a heavy pot, layer chicken, rice, fried onion, fresh mint, and saffron mixed with warm milk.
Seal the pot tightly with foil and a lid. Cook on high heat for 5 minutes, then lowest heat for 25 minutes (dum cooking).
Open at the table. Gently mix from the bottom and serve with raita.

name: Baklava
description: Crispy filo pastry layered with walnuts and drenched in honey-rose syrup.

steps.text: Make syrup: boil water, sugar, and honey for 5 minutes. Add rose water. Cool completely.
Roughly chop walnuts and mix with cinnamon and a little sugar.
Brush a baking tray with butter. Layer 6–8 filo sheets, brushing each with butter.
Spread walnut mixture evenly. Continue layering filo with butter on top.
Cut into diamonds all the way through before baking. Bake at 180°C for 35–40 minutes until golden.
Immediately pour cold syrup over hot baklava. Let absorb for at least 2 hours before serving.

name: Souvlaki (Greek Grilled Pork Skewers)
description: Bite-sized pork marinated in lemon, garlic, and oregano and grilled on skewers — one of the most common fast, everyday meals across Greece.

steps.text: Cut the pork into 2-3cm cubes.
Mince the garlic and whisk together with lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Toss the pork in the marinade and let sit for at least 15 minutes, or up to a few hours in the fridge.
Thread the pork onto skewers.
Grill over high heat, turning occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Serve hot on or off the skewer, with warm pita.

name: Strukli (Croatian Cheese Pastry)
description: Croatian baked or boiled pastry filled with cottage cheese, eggs, and cream.

steps.text: Make soft dough from flour, egg, oil, and warm water. Knead until smooth. Rest 30 minutes.
Mix cottage cheese with eggs, sour cream, and salt for the filling.
Roll dough very thin on a floured cloth. Spread filling evenly over the dough.
Using the cloth, roll the dough into a log. Slice into portions.
Boil in salted water for 10 minutes, then transfer to a baking dish.
Pour sour cream over the top. Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until golden.

name: Mushroom Omelette
description: Fluffy French-style omelette folded around sautéed mushrooms and melted cheese.

components.name: butter
components.comment: 10 g for mushrooms; 5 g for eggs

steps.text: Slice the mushrooms and cook in 10 g butter over medium-high heat until golden and their moisture has evaporated. Set aside.
Whisk the 3 eggs with the measured salt and pepper.
Melt the remaining 5 g butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat and pour in the eggs.
Gently draw the set egg towards the centre while tilting the pan to fill the gaps with uncooked egg.
When almost set, add the mushrooms, grated cheddar and chopped chives to one half. Fold over and serve immediately.

name: Philadelphia Roll
description: Inside-out roll filled with salmon, cream cheese, and creamy avocado.

steps.text: Cook and season sushi rice. Let cool to body temperature.
Place nori on a bamboo mat. Spread a thin, even layer of rice over the nori, right to the edges.
Flip the sheet over so rice faces down. Sprinkle sesame seeds on the rice.
Place cream cheese, salmon strips, avocado, and cucumber along the near edge of the nori.
Roll tightly using the mat. Seal the edge with a damp finger.
Slice with a very sharp wet knife into 8 pieces. Serve with soy sauce and wasabi.

name: Halva (Balkan Semolina Dessert)
description: Sweet Greek-style semolina halva with olive oil, pine nuts, and cinnamon.

steps.text: Make syrup: combine sugar, water, cinnamon sticks, and cloves. Bring to boil and simmer 5 minutes.
In a separate pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add pine nuts and fry briefly until golden.
Add semolina and stir constantly over medium heat for 5–7 minutes until it turns a deep golden colour.
Step back and carefully pour the hot syrup into the semolina — it will bubble vigorously.
Stir quickly until all liquid is absorbed. Cover and rest for 5 minutes.
Press into moulds or a bowl. Invert onto a plate. Dust with cinnamon and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Bratwurst with Sauerkraut
description: Grilled pork bratwurst served with tangy sauerkraut and wholegrain mustard.

steps.text: Simmer bratwurst in beer and sliced onion for 10 minutes (this adds flavour and prevents splitting).
Remove from liquid and grill or pan-fry until golden brown on all sides.
Meanwhile, heat sauerkraut with a splash of the beer liquid and caraway seeds for 5 minutes.
Serve bratwurst on sauerkraut with wholegrain mustard. Optionally add pretzel bread.

name: Pyure s Kotletoy (Mashed Potato with Meat Cutlet)
description: Homemade pan-fried meat cutlets served over buttery mashed potato — a default weeknight dinner across Russia and Ukraine.

steps.text: Soak the breadcrumbs in milk for 5 minutes. Finely grate or mince the onion.
Mix the beef mince, soaked breadcrumbs, onion, egg, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Shape into 4-6 oval patties with wet hands.
Fry the cutlets in vegetable oil over medium heat, 5-6 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain and mash the potatoes with butter and a splash of hot milk until smooth.
Serve the cutlets over the mashed potato.

name: Hummus with Pita
description: Silky chickpea and tahini dip drizzled with olive oil, served with warm pita bread.

steps.text: Drain canned chickpeas and reserve the liquid (aquafaba).
Blend chickpeas with tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and salt until very smooth.
Add a few tablespoons of aquafaba or ice water and blend again — this makes it extra fluffy.
Taste and adjust: more lemon, salt, or tahini to your preference.
Spread in a bowl, drizzle with olive oil, and dust with paprika or cumin. Serve with warm pita.

name: Plov (Pilaf)
description: Festive Uzbek rice dish slow-cooked with lamb, carrots, and fragrant cumin.

steps.text: Heat oil in a heavy pot (kazan). Fry onion slices until deep golden.
Add cubed lamb and fry until browned on all sides.
Add julienned carrots and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with cumin, coriander, salt, and pepper. Press a whole head of garlic into the centre.
Spread washed and soaked rice evenly on top. Add boiling water to cover by 2 cm.
Cook uncovered on high until water disappears. Make holes in rice with a spoon handle.
Cover tightly, reduce to lowest heat, and steam for 25–30 minutes. Fluff and serve.

name: Fish and Chips
description: Beer-battered cod with thick-cut chips and tartare sauce — British pub classic.

steps.text: Cut potatoes into thick chips. Double-fry: first at 160°C for 5 minutes, then at 190°C for 3 minutes until golden.
Make batter: whisk flour, baking powder, salt, and cold beer until smooth.
Pat cod dry, season, and dust lightly with flour.
Dip in batter and fry at 180°C for 5–6 minutes until batter is puffed and golden.
Drain on paper towels. Serve with hot chips, tartare sauce, lemon, and malt vinegar.

name: Homestyle Meat Patties
description: Juicy pan-fried minced pork patties with onion and soaked bread, a staple comfort dish.

steps.text: Soak white bread in milk for 5 minutes. Squeeze out excess milk.
Combine pork mince, soaked bread, finely grated onion, garlic, egg, salt, and pepper.
Knead mixture for 2–3 minutes until well combined and slightly sticky.
Shape into oval patties with wet hands.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry patties for 5–6 minutes per side until golden brown.
Cover and cook on low for 3 more minutes to ensure they're cooked through. Serve with mashed potato.

name: Tom Yum Soup
description: Fragrant Thai soup with lemongrass, galangal, mushrooms, and prawns in spicy broth.

steps.text: Bruise lemongrass stalks and slice galangal. Simmer in chicken broth for 10 minutes to infuse.
Add kaffir lime leaves, sliced mushrooms, and Thai chili to the broth.
Add prawns and cook for 2–3 minutes until pink.
Season with fish sauce and a generous squeeze of lime juice.
Taste and adjust: it should be sour, salty, and spicy. Garnish with cilantro and serve.

name: Clam Chowder
description: Creamy New England soup packed with clams, potato, bacon, and celery.

steps.text: Cook bacon in a pot until crispy. Remove and set aside, leaving fat in pot.
Sauté diced onion and celery in bacon fat until soft.
Add flour and stir for 1 minute to make a roux.
Add clam juice and diced potato. Simmer until potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
Add cream and clams. Heat gently — do not boil after adding cream.
Season with salt, pepper, and thyme. Serve topped with bacon and oyster crackers.

name: Guacamole
description: Creamy smashed avocado with lime, cilantro, red onion, and fresh chili.

steps.text: Halve and pit avocados. Scoop flesh into a bowl.
Mash with a fork to desired texture — leave it a little chunky.
Finely dice red onion, jalapeño, and tomato. Chop cilantro.
Fold everything in with a squeeze of lime juice and a generous pinch of salt.
Taste and adjust: more lime for brightness, more salt to season. Serve immediately with tortilla chips.

name: Ajvar Bruschetta
description: Balkan-style toast topped with smoky roasted red pepper ajvar and fresh herbs.

steps.text: Slice rustic bread and toast until golden and crispy.
Rub each slice lightly with a raw garlic clove.
Spread ajvar generously on each slice.
Drizzle with olive oil and scatter fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

name: Makarna (Turkish Tomato Pasta)
description: Everyday Turkish pasta stirred through with a simple tomato and butter sauce — quick comfort food for weeknights.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente. Drain.
Finely dice the onion and cook in butter over medium heat until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes until it darkens slightly.
Add water and simmer for 5 minutes to form a light sauce.
Toss the drained pasta through the sauce, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.

name: Blini with Sour Cream
description: Classic thin Russian pancakes served with sour cream, butter, and honey.

steps.text: Whisk together eggs, warm milk, melted butter, sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Gradually mix in flour until you have a smooth, thin, lump-free batter. Rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a small crepe pan over medium-high heat. Brush lightly with butter.
Pour a small ladleful of batter and immediately swirl pan to spread thinly.
Cook for 60–90 seconds until edges lift and surface looks dry. Flip and cook 30 more seconds.
Stack blini and serve with sour cream, butter, honey, or jam.

name: BLT Sandwich
description: The perfect combo of crispy bacon, fresh lettuce, and tomato on toasted white bread.

steps.text: Cook bacon in a dry pan until extra crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Toast bread until golden.
Spread mayo on both slices of toast.
Layer lettuce, tomato slices, and bacon. Season tomato with salt and pepper.
Press together, cut diagonally. Serve immediately.

name: Moussaka
description: Greek layered casserole of minced lamb, eggplant, and béchamel, baked golden.

steps.text: Slice eggplant, salt and drain for 20 minutes. Pat dry and fry or roast until golden.
Make meat sauce: brown lamb mince with onion, add tomatoes, cinnamon, allspice, bay leaf. Simmer 20 minutes.
Make thick béchamel. Remove from heat and whisk in egg yolk and a handful of parmesan.
Layer in a baking dish: eggplant → meat sauce → eggplant → meat sauce → béchamel.
Dust with parmesan and nutmeg. Bake at 180°C for 45 minutes until deeply golden on top.
Essential: rest for 20–30 minutes before cutting, or it will fall apart.

name: Badrijani Nigvzit (Eggplant Rolls with Walnut Paste)
description: Thin fried eggplant slices rolled around a garlicky walnut paste — a classic cold starter served at nearly every Georgian gathering, big or small.

steps.text: Slice the eggplant lengthwise into thin strips, salt lightly, and let sit for 10 minutes to draw out bitterness. Pat dry.
Fry the eggplant strips in oil over medium heat for 2-3 minutes per side until soft and golden. Drain on paper towels.
Crush the walnuts and garlic into a paste, then mix in vinegar, khmeli-suneli, and salt to make a thick spread.
Spread a small spoonful of the walnut paste along one end of each eggplant strip and roll up.
Arrange on a plate, garnish with cilantro, and serve at room temperature.

name: Chicken Teriyaki Bowl
description: Glazed teriyaki chicken on steamed rice with sesame seeds and spring onion.

steps.text: Mix soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar to make teriyaki sauce.
Score chicken thighs and pan-fry skin-side down over medium-high heat for 5–6 minutes.
Flip and cook another 4 minutes. Pour in teriyaki sauce and simmer until thick and glossy.
Cook steamed rice according to packet.
Slice chicken and serve over rice. Spoon sauce on top, garnish with sesame and green onion.

name: Apple Pie
description: Classic American double-crust apple pie with cinnamon spiced filling.

components.name: sugar
components.comment: 80 g for filling; 10 g for topping

components.name: pie pastry
components.comment: ready-made vegetarian butter pastry for a base and lid

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Divide the ready-made pastry in half. Roll one half to line a 23 cm pie dish and keep the other half chilled for the lid.
Slice the peeled, cored apples. Toss with 80 g sugar, cinnamon, 20 g flour and lemon juice.
Spoon the filling into the pastry case and dot with the 20 g butter.
Roll out the remaining pastry, cover the pie and seal the edges. Cut several steam vents in the lid.
Brush with 15 g beaten egg and sprinkle with the remaining 10 g sugar.
Bake for 20 minutes at 200°C, then reduce to 175°C and bake for another 35–40 minutes, until golden and bubbling. Cool for about 2 hours before cutting into 8 slices.

name: Quiche Lorraine
description: Classic French tart with a silky cream, egg, and smoked bacon filling.

steps.text: Line a tart tin with shortcrust pastry. Chill for 15 minutes.
Blind bake pastry at 180°C for 15 minutes (line with paper and beans). Remove beans, bake 5 more minutes.
Fry bacon lardons until golden. Drain and scatter over pastry base with grated Gruyère.
Whisk together eggs, double cream, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Pour custard into the tart shell. Bake at 160°C for 30–35 minutes until just set with a slight wobble.
Cool slightly before slicing. Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Chocolate Mousse
description: Light and airy dark chocolate mousse with a just-set wobble, topped with cream.

steps.text: Melt dark chocolate with butter over a bain-marie. Stir smooth and cool slightly.
Separate eggs. Whisk yolks with sugar until pale. Mix into chocolate.
Whip cream to soft peaks. Whip egg whites to stiff peaks.
Fold cream into chocolate mixture, then gently fold in egg whites in two additions.
Pour into serving glasses. Refrigerate at least 3 hours.
Serve with a dollop of lightly whipped cream and chocolate shavings.

name: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
description: Tender chicken pieces simmered in a rich, mildly spiced tomato-cream sauce.

steps.text: Marinate chicken in yogurt, garam masala, ginger-garlic paste, and salt for 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-fry marinated chicken until slightly charred. Set aside.
Sauté onion in butter until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 2 minutes. Add canned tomatoes and garam masala. Simmer 15 minutes.
Blend sauce until smooth. Pass through a sieve for silky texture.
Return sauce to pan. Add cream and crumbled dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi). Simmer gently.
Add grilled chicken pieces and simmer 10 minutes. Serve with naan or basmati rice.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Grilled chicken tikka pieces simmered in a rich, aromatic spiced tomato-cream sauce.

steps.text: Marinate chicken chunks in yogurt, tikka masala spice, and lemon juice for 1–2 hours.
Grill marinated chicken under a hot broiler until slightly charred. Set aside.
Fry onion in butter until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and fry 2 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes and spices. Simmer 15 minutes.
Blend the sauce until smooth. Return to pan, add cream.
Add grilled chicken and simmer 10 minutes. Serve with basmati rice and naan.

name: Cheeseburger
description: Juicy beef patty with melted cheddar, fresh vegetables, and classic burger sauce.

steps.text: Form ground beef into a patty slightly larger than the bun (it will shrink). Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat a cast iron pan over high heat. Cook patty for 3–4 minutes per side for medium.
Place a slice of cheddar on the patty in the last minute. Cover to melt.
Toast bun halves in the same pan.
Build: sauce on bottom bun, lettuce, tomato, patty with cheese, pickles, top bun. Serve.

name: Chicken Noodle Soup
description: Light golden broth with tender chicken, homemade noodles, and fresh herbs.

steps.text: Place chicken in a large pot with cold water. Add whole onion, carrot, parsley root, bay leaf, and peppercorns.
Bring to a boil, skim foam carefully. Simmer on low for 40–50 minutes.
Remove chicken and vegetables. Strain the broth until clear.
Slice the carrot from the broth. Shred the chicken meat.
Bring broth back to a boil. Add egg noodles and cook 3–4 minutes. Return chicken and carrot.
Season with salt. Serve with fresh dill and a grind of black pepper.

name: Caprese Salad
description: Sliced ripe tomatoes and fresh mozzarella with basil, balsamic, and olive oil.

steps.text: Slice tomatoes and mozzarella into rounds of equal thickness.
Alternate tomato and mozzarella slices on a platter.
Tuck fresh basil leaves between the slices.
Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil and balsamic glaze. Season with sea salt and black pepper.

name: Zharenaya Kartoshka (Fried Potatoes with Onion)
description: Golden pan-fried potatoes with plenty of onion — a staple side or light dinner in almost every Russian household.

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and slice into thin rounds or matchsticks. Pat dry with a towel.
Heat oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add the potatoes in a single layer and fry without stirring for 5 minutes to let them crisp.
Slice the onion and add it to the pan. Stir occasionally and cook for 12-15 minutes until the potatoes are golden and tender.
Season with salt and pepper in the last few minutes, then top with dill and serve hot.

name: Olivier Salad
description: Classic Russian holiday salad with boiled sausage, potatoes, eggs, and mayo.

steps.text: Boil potatoes and carrots (with skins on) until tender. Cool completely, then peel and dice small.
Hard-boil eggs for 10 minutes. Cool, peel, and dice.
Dice bologna sausage and pickled cucumbers into small even pieces.
Drain canned peas.
Combine all ingredients in a bowl. Fold in mayonnaise until well coated.
Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving for flavours to meld.

name: Chakhokhbili (Georgian Chicken Stew)
description: Georgian braised chicken stewed in tomatoes with garlic, herbs, and khmeli-suneli.

steps.text: Brown chicken pieces dry in a heavy pan — no oil — over high heat until golden. This is the Georgian technique.
Add sliced onion and sauté 5 minutes. Add butter.
Add grated or diced ripe tomatoes. Cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Add garlic, adjika, and khmeli-suneli. Season with salt.
Simmer uncovered 10 more minutes until sauce thickens. Finish with a generous handful of cilantro and parsley.

name: Khinkali (Georgian Soup Dumplings)
description: Hand-pleated dumplings filled with spiced, juicy meat and broth — a staple at nearly every Georgian family table, eaten by hand and never with a fork.

steps.text: Mix the flour, water, and a pinch of salt into a firm dough. Knead for 8 minutes, then rest covered for 30 minutes.
Grate the onion and mix it with the beef, pork, cilantro, cumin, pepper, and salt.
Add a splash of cold water to the filling and mix well so it becomes juicy and loose.
Roll the dough thin and cut into 10cm circles.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, then pleat the edges around the filling, twisting to seal at the top into a small knob.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil and drop in the dumplings in batches, stirring gently so they don't stick.
Boil for 10-12 minutes until they float and the dough is cooked through.
Lift out with a slotted spoon, dust with black pepper, and serve hot, holding by the knob to eat.

name: Pide
description: Turkish boat-shaped flatbread filled with spiced beef mince and melted cheese.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 230°C with baking stone inside.
Make filling: brown ground beef with diced onion, pepper, and tomato. Season with cumin and chili. Cool slightly.
Roll dough into an oval shape. Score the edges to form a boat, folding sides up.
Fill centre with meat mixture. Grate kaşar cheese generously on top.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until edges are golden and cheese is melted.
Brush edges with melted butter and finish with a raw egg in the centre if desired. Serve with parsley and lemon.

name: Hungarian Goulash
description: Hearty paprika-rich beef and potato stew, the soul of Hungarian cuisine.

steps.text: Cut the beef into cubes. Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches, about 10 minutes in total. Remove to a plate.
Dice the onion and pepper and cook in the same pot for 5 minutes. Take off the heat and stir in the sweet and hot paprika.
Return the beef and add the stock, tomato paste, caraway seeds and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer for 60–70 minutes, until the beef is almost tender.
Add diced potatoes and carrots and simmer for another 20 minutes, until tender. Add a little water if the pot becomes too dry.
Remove the bay leaf and stir in the measured salt and pepper. Divide into 4 portions. Extra bread or noodles is optional and is not included in the quantities.

name: Fërgesë (Albanian Pepper Stew)
description: Albanian oven-baked stew of roasted peppers, tomatoes, and creamy cottage cheese.

steps.text: Roast peppers over a flame or under a broiler until charred. Peel and slice.
Dice tomatoes. Sauté in olive oil with chili for 5 minutes.
Add roasted peppers. Mix well and transfer to an oven dish.
Dot cottage cheese over the surface.
Bake at 190°C for 25–30 minutes until the cheese melts into the sauce.
Scatter fresh basil. Serve hot with bread for scooping.

name: Okroshka
description: Refreshing cold Russian soup with kvass, vegetables, egg, and sausage.

steps.text: Dice cucumber, radish, and bologna into small even cubes. Chop hard-boiled eggs.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl or soup pot.
Season with salt, a pinch of mustard, and a squeeze of lemon.
Pour cold kvass over everything until submerged. Stir.
Serve immediately in chilled bowls with a large spoonful of sour cream and fresh dill.

name: Dolma (Turkish Stuffed Vine Leaves)
description: Tender vine leaves stuffed with herbed rice, pine nuts, and currants, served cold.

steps.text: Sauté diced onion until soft. Add raw rice, pine nuts, currants, and spices. Cook 2 minutes.
Rinse vine leaves in hot water to soften. Pat dry.
Place a vine leaf vein-side up. Add a small amount of filling. Fold sides in and roll tightly.
Pack tightly in a pot, seam-side down. Add olive oil, lemon juice, and water to just cover.
Weight down with a plate. Simmer on low heat for 45 minutes.
Cool completely in the pot. Serve at room temperature with lemon wedges and yogurt.

name: Smoothie Bowl
description: Thick blended mango and berry smoothie topped with granola, banana, and coconut.

steps.text: Blend frozen banana, berries, and mango with minimal liquid — the base should be very thick.
Pour into a bowl and smooth the surface.
Arrange toppings in neat sections: granola, sliced fresh fruit, coconut flakes, chia seeds.
Serve immediately before the base melts.

name: Miso Soup
description: Delicate Japanese broth with silken tofu, wakame seaweed, and green onion.

steps.text: Bring dashi stock to a gentle simmer (do not boil).
Rehydrate dried wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Dissolve miso paste in a ladle of hot stock, then stir back into the pot.
Add cubed tofu and wakame. Heat gently for 1 minute without boiling.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with sliced green onion. Serve immediately.

name: Tavče Gravče (Macedonian Baked Beans)
description: Hearty Macedonian national dish of white beans baked with peppers and paprika.

steps.text: Soak dried white beans overnight, then boil until tender but not falling apart.
Sauté diced onion in oil until golden. Add diced roasted peppers, tomato, and paprika.
Mix onion mixture with drained beans. Season with salt and chili.
Transfer to a clay pot (or oven dish). Add a ladle of the cooking liquid.
Bake at 200°C for 30–40 minutes until the top is lightly browned and beans have absorbed the sauce.
Garnish with fresh parsley. Serve in the clay pot with crusty bread.

name: French Onion Soup
description: Deeply caramelised onion broth topped with crusty bread and melted Gruyère.

steps.text: Slice onions thinly. Melt butter in a heavy pot and add onions with a pinch of salt.
Cook on medium-low heat for 35–45 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until onions are deep golden.
Deglaze with white wine, scraping up browned bits. Add stock, thyme, and bay leaf.
Simmer for 15 minutes. Season with salt, pepper, and a splash of brandy if desired.
Ladle into oven-safe bowls. Place a baguette slice on top. Cover with grated Gruyère.
Broil under high heat for 3–4 minutes until cheese is bubbling and slightly charred.

name: Musaka (Balkan Potato Musaka)
description: Balkan layered casserole of minced meat and potato with egg-cream topping.

steps.text: Thinly slice potatoes. Brown pork mince with diced onion, tomato, and paprika.
Layer raw potato slices and meat mixture alternately in an oiled baking dish. Season each layer.
Pour a little water or broth over to prevent drying out.
Bake at 190°C for 40 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Whisk eggs with yogurt and sour cream. Pour over the musaka.
Bake another 20–25 minutes until topping is set and golden. Rest 10 minutes.

name: Fresh Spring Rolls
description: Rice paper rolls stuffed with vegetables, mint, rice noodles, and dipping sauce.

steps.text: Cook rice vermicelli according to package. Rinse in cold water and drain well.
Julienne carrot and cucumber. Slice avocado thinly.
Fill a large bowl with warm water. Dip one rice paper for 10–15 seconds until soft.
Lay on a damp surface. Place herbs first, then noodles and vegetables on the lower third.
Fold bottom up, fold sides in, and roll forward tightly. Serve with peanut-hoisin dipping sauce.

name: Tuna Melt Sandwich
description: Open-faced tuna salad sandwich topped with melted cheese, grilled until golden.

steps.text: Drain tuna well. Mix with mayonnaise, finely diced celery and red onion, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Toast bread until golden.
Spread tuna mixture on toast. Cover generously with grated cheddar.
Grill or broil for 3–4 minutes until cheese is bubbling and golden. Serve hot.

name: Phở Bò
description: Vietnamese clear beef broth with rice noodles, star anise, and fresh herbs.

steps.text: Blanch beef bones in boiling water for 5 minutes. Rinse.
Char ginger and onion directly over a flame or under a broiler. Add to bones with fresh water.
Toast star anise, cinnamon, and cloves in a dry pan. Wrap in muslin and add to broth.
Simmer on very low heat for 3–4 hours, skimming foam. Season with fish sauce and salt.
Cook rice noodles in boiling water. Divide into bowls. Add thinly sliced raw beef.
Ladle boiling hot broth over noodles — it cooks the beef instantly. Serve with herbs, sprouts, lime, and hoisin.

name: Onigiri (Rice Balls)
description: Simple salted rice balls wrapped in nori — an everyday Japanese snack or lunchbox item.

steps.text: Cook the sushi rice according to package instructions and let it cool slightly, until warm but workable.
Mix the tuna with mayonnaise for the filling.
Wet your hands with water and a little salt, then take a handful of rice and flatten it in your palm.
Add a spoonful of filling in the center and fold the rice around it, shaping into a triangle.
Press gently to compact, wrap a strip of nori around the base, and repeat with remaining rice.

name: Roasted Red Pepper Soup
description: Velvety blended red pepper and tomato soup with smoked paprika and cream.

components.name: cream
components.comment: single cream, about 18% fat; 80 ml in soup and 20 ml for serving

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Halve and deseed the peppers. Roast cut-side down for about 25 minutes, until the skin is charred, then peel.
Dice the onion and cook in the olive oil for 8 minutes. Add chopped garlic and smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the canned tomatoes, roasted peppers and stock. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend until smooth. Stir in 80 ml cream, salt and pepper and heat gently without boiling.
Divide into 4 bowls and finish with the remaining 20 ml cream. Extra bread is optional and is not included in the quantities.

name: Sloppy Joe
description: Ground beef simmered in a sweet-tangy tomato sauce and piled onto a soft bun — a fast, messy American weeknight sandwich kids and adults both grew up eating.

steps.text: Finely dice the onion.
Heat oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the beef mince and cook, breaking it up, until browned, about 6 minutes.
Stir in ketchup, tomato paste, mustard, brown sugar, and salt.
Add a splash of water and simmer for 8-10 minutes until thickened and saucy.
Spoon generously onto toasted buns and serve immediately.

name: Stuffed Cabbage Rolls (Holubtsi)
description: Tender cabbage leaves stuffed with pork and rice, braised in tomato sauce.

steps.text: Core the cabbage. Blanch whole head in boiling water for 3–4 minutes. Peel off softened outer leaves and repeat.
Mix pork mince with par-cooked rice, sautéed onion, salt, and pepper.
Place filling on each leaf and roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Make sauce: fry grated carrot and onion, add tomato paste, stock, and sour cream.
Arrange rolls tightly in a pot. Pour sauce over. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 50–60 minutes. Serve with extra sour cream.

name: Vinaigrette Salad
description: Colourful Russian salad of beetroot, carrot, potato, pickles, and peas in oil.

steps.text: Boil beetroot, carrot, and potato separately with skins on until tender. Cool completely, then peel.
Dice all vegetables and pickled cucumbers into small, even cubes.
Dice onion very finely. Drain canned peas.
Combine everything in a bowl. Dress with vegetable oil, a splash of vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Stir gently and refrigerate for 30 minutes. The beetroot will colour everything pink — that's normal.

name: Roast Red Pepper Soup
description: Velvety blended red pepper and tomato soup with smoked paprika and cream.

components.name: cream
components.comment: single cream, about 18% fat; 80 ml in soup and 20 ml for serving

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Halve the peppers and remove their seeds. Roast cut-side down for about 25 minutes, until the skin is charred, then peel.
Dice the onion and cook in the olive oil for 8 minutes. Add chopped garlic and smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, roasted peppers and stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend until smooth. Return to the pan and stir in 80 ml cream, salt and pepper. Heat gently without boiling.
Divide into 4 bowls and finish with the remaining 20 ml cream. Extra croutons are optional and are not included in the quantities.

name: Sushi Set
description: Assorted nigiri and rolls with salmon, tuna, and avocado served with soy sauce.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and cook with the measured water according to the packet instructions, about 20 minutes.
Dissolve the sugar and salt in the rice vinegar. Fold into the hot rice and spread out to cool for about 20 minutes.
Keep the fish refrigerated until assembly. Use fish suitable for raw preparation; cut some into strips for rolls and the rest into thin slices for nigiri.
Slice the avocado. Spread part of the rice over the nori, add fish strips and avocado, roll tightly and cut into pieces.
Shape the remaining rice into small oblongs and top with the remaining fish. Divide the rolls and nigiri into 3 portions and serve promptly with the measured soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger.

name: Manestra (Balkan Rice and Tomato Soup)
description: Simple Croatian comfort soup of rice, tomato, and herbs — like a hug in a bowl.

steps.text: Sauté diced onion and garlic in olive oil until soft.
Add canned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add vegetable stock and bring to a boil.
Add rice and cook for 15–18 minutes until tender.
Season with salt and pepper. Stir in fresh parsley. Drizzle with olive oil and serve.

name: Avocado Toast
description: Sourdough toast topped with smashed avocado, chili flakes, lemon, and sea salt.

steps.text: Toast sourdough slices until golden and crispy.
Halve avocado, remove pit, and scoop flesh into a bowl.
Mash with a fork, add lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Leave slightly chunky.
Spread avocado generously on toast. Finish with chili flakes, flaky sea salt, and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Chicken Curry
description: Aromatic Thai curry with tender chicken, coconut milk, and fragrant spices.

steps.text: Fry curry paste in a dry pan for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Add a splash of coconut milk and cook, stirring, until the paste starts to separate.
Add chicken pieces and coat in the paste. Cook for 3–4 minutes.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk. Add fish sauce, palm sugar, and kaffir lime leaves.
Simmer on medium heat for 20 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Stir in Thai basil just before serving over steamed rice.

name: Dal (Indian Lentil Curry)
description: Warming spiced red lentil stew with tomatoes, cumin, turmeric, and fresh ginger.

steps.text: Rinse the lentils. Place in a saucepan with the water and turmeric. Bring to a boil and simmer for about 20 minutes, until soft.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a frying pan. Add the cumin and mustard seeds and cook until fragrant. Add diced onion and cook for 8 minutes.
Add finely chopped garlic and ginger, then the canned tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes.
Stir the tomato mixture into the lentils and simmer for 5–10 minutes. Add water if needed for a spoonable consistency.
Stir in the lemon juice and salt. Divide into 3 portions. Extra rice or bread is optional and is not included in these quantities.

name: Bratkartoffeln (German Fried Potatoes)
description: Pan-fried potatoes with crispy edges and bacon and onion — the everyday German side dish that often becomes the whole meal.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes whole in salted water until just tender, about 15 minutes. Cool, peel, and slice.
Dice the bacon and onion.
Fry the bacon in a large pan until crisp, then remove and set aside.
Add butter and oil to the same pan, then fry the potato slices in a single layer until golden, about 8 minutes per side.
Add the onion in the last 5 minutes of frying, along with the bacon.
Season with salt and pepper, scatter with parsley, and serve hot.

name: Club Sandwich
description: Triple-decker toasted sandwich with chicken, bacon, lettuce, tomato, and mayo.

steps.text: Season chicken breast and grill or pan-fry until cooked through. Rest and slice.
Cook bacon until crispy. Toast three slices of bread.
Spread mayo on all three toast slices.
First layer: lettuce, tomato, chicken on bottom toast. Add middle toast.
Second layer: bacon, more lettuce. Top with the third slice of toast.
Secure with four toothpicks and cut diagonally into four triangles.

name: Buckwheat with Fried Onion
description: Nutty roasted buckwheat groats topped with golden caramelised onion and butter.

steps.text: Toast buckwheat in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes until it smells nutty.
Add boiling salted water (2:1 ratio). Cover and cook on lowest heat for 15 minutes. Do not lift the lid.
Meanwhile, slice onion thinly and fry in oil over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring, until golden brown.
Fluff buckwheat with a fork and add a knob of butter.
Serve topped with caramelised onion. Great with a fried egg or sour cream.

name: Kharcho (Georgian Spiced Beef and Rice Soup)
description: Tangy, garlicky beef soup thickened with rice and warmed with khmeli-suneli — a hearty everyday soup found on the stove in Georgian homes year-round.

steps.text: Cut the beef into small cubes and simmer in 1.2 liters of water for 30 minutes, skimming any foam, until nearly tender.
Dice the onion and add it to the pot along with the rice.
Simmer for 12 minutes until the rice is cooked.
Mince the garlic and crush the walnuts finely.
Stir in the tomato paste, garlic, walnuts, khmeli-suneli, and adjika.
Simmer for another 5 minutes to let the flavors meld, then season with salt and stir in cilantro before serving.

name: Bigos (Polish Hunter's Stew)
description: Polish national dish of sauerkraut, mixed meats, dried mushrooms, and sausage.

steps.text: Soak dried mushrooms in warm water 30 minutes. Drain and slice, reserving soaking liquid.
Brown cubed pork and sliced kielbasa in batches in a large pot. Remove.
Add shredded fresh cabbage to the pot, cook until wilted. Add sauerkraut, mushrooms and soaking liquid, tomato paste, red wine, bay leaf, and allspice.
Return all meat. Add water to barely cover. Season with salt and pepper.
Simmer covered on low heat for 90 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Bigos is traditionally made in large batches and reheated several times — it gets better each day.

name: BBQ Ribs
description: Slow-cooked pork ribs glazed with smoky-sweet BBQ sauce until fall-off-the-bone tender.

steps.text: Remove the membrane from the back of the ribs.
Mix dry rub: paprika, garlic powder, brown sugar, salt, pepper, and mustard. Coat ribs generously. Refrigerate overnight.
Preheat oven to 150°C. Wrap ribs tightly in foil and bake for 2.5–3 hours until very tender.
Open foil, brush ribs with BBQ sauce.
Grill or broil for 5–10 minutes until sauce is sticky and caramelised.
Rest 5 minutes. Cut between bones and serve with coleslaw.

name: Roštilj (Balkan Mixed Grill)
description: Balkan-style mixed grill of ćevapi and chicken skewers with flatbread, onion, ajvar and sour cream.

components.name: garlic
components.comment: 6 g for mince; 4 g for chicken

components.name: salt
components.comment: 3 g for mince; 1 g for chicken

steps.text: Mix the beef and pork with 6 g crushed garlic, baking soda, 3 g salt and 0.5 g pepper. Shape into small ćevapi fingers, cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Cut the chicken into chunks and coat with the oil, paprika, remaining garlic, salt and pepper. Refrigerate alongside the ćevapi.
Thread the chicken onto skewers. Grill both meats for about 15–20 minutes, turning regularly, until cooked through.
Warm the flatbreads and finely chop the onion. Divide the meats, onion, ajvar and sour cream into 4 portions.

name: Ćevapi
description: Balkan skinless grilled sausages made of beef and lamb, served with flatbread and onion.

steps.text: Mix beef and lamb mince with grated garlic, baking soda, salt, and pepper. Knead vigorously for 5 minutes.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours (overnight is better) — resting develops the flavour and texture.
Shape into small cylinders about the size of a finger using wet hands.
Grill on a very hot charcoal or ridged grill for 8–10 minutes, turning to cook all sides.
Serve in a warmed flatbread (lepinja) with finely diced raw onion, sour cream, and ajvar.

name: Beef Wok Noodles
description: Stir-fried egg noodles with strips of beef, broccoli, and oyster sauce.

steps.text: Slice beef very thin against the grain. Marinate in soy sauce, cornstarch, and a little oil.
Cook egg noodles until just done. Drain and rinse with cold water.
Heat wok over maximum heat until smoking. Sear beef in batches quickly, 60–90 seconds. Remove.
Add garlic and ginger to wok. Add broccoli and pepper, stir-fry 2–3 minutes.
Add noodles and oyster sauce. Toss everything together over high heat for 2 minutes.
Return beef, toss once more. Drizzle with sesame oil and serve.

name: Currywurst
description: Berlin street food: sliced pork sausage smothered in curried ketchup sauce.

components.name: curry powder
components.comment: 3 g for sauce; 1 g for finishing

steps.text: Heat the fully cooked sausages in a non-stick pan or under a grill for 10–15 minutes, turning occasionally, until hot throughout.
Meanwhile, combine the ketchup, 3 g curry powder, paprika, Worcestershire sauce, sugar and water. Simmer gently for 3–5 minutes.
Slice the sausages onto 2 plates, spoon over the sauce and finish with the remaining curry powder. Extra fries or bread are optional and are not included in these quantities.

name: Stovetop Mac and Cheese
description: Quick homemade macaroni and cheese made in one pot — everyday American comfort food, no baking required.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente. Drain.
In the same pot, melt the butter over medium heat and whisk in the flour, cooking for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the milk and cook, stirring, until thickened, about 4 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in the cheddar until melted and smooth.
Fold the pasta back into the cheese sauce, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.

name: Tamagoyaki (Japanese Rolled Omelette)
description: Lightly sweet rolled Japanese omelette — a quick everyday breakfast or lunchbox staple.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with soy sauce, sugar, and dashi until smooth.
Heat a little oil in a rectangular or regular nonstick pan over medium-low heat.
Pour in a thin layer of egg mixture, and once mostly set, roll it up to one side of the pan.
Oil the empty part of the pan, pour in more egg mixture, lifting the rolled egg so it flows underneath, then roll again.
Repeat until all the egg mixture is used, forming a multi-layered roll.
Let it rest for a minute, then slice into pieces and serve.

name: Pasulj (Serbian Bean Stew)
description: Everyday Balkan bean stew simmered with onion, paprika, and a little smoked meat — a Sunday-to-Friday staple.

steps.text: If using dried beans, ensure they've been soaked overnight and drained; if using canned, drain and rinse.
Dice the onion, carrot, and bacon.
Heat oil in a pot and fry the bacon until it releases its fat, then add onion and carrot and cook until soft, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the paprika and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans, bay leaf, and enough water to cover by 2cm. Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and let it thicken slightly before serving with bread.

name: Spinach and Feta Börek
description: Turkish crispy fried filo pastries filled with spinach, feta, and herbs.

steps.text: Thaw and squeeze out all moisture from spinach. Mix with crumbled feta, dill, and a beaten egg.
Cut filo into strips about 8 cm wide. Brush with olive oil.
Place a spoonful of filling at one end of a filo strip. Fold into a triangle, flipping over and over to the end.
Brush triangles with oil.
Either bake at 190°C for 20–25 minutes until golden, or pan-fry in shallow oil for 2–3 minutes per side.

name: Pašticada (Dalmatian Pot Roast)
description: Dalmatian-style braised beef in a wine, vegetable and prune sauce.

steps.text: Make small slits in the beef and insert garlic pieces. Place in a covered non-reactive dish with the wine, chopped carrot and onion, rosemary and cloves. Refrigerate for 8 hours.
Remove and pat dry the beef, reserving all marinade and vegetables. Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef for about 10 minutes.
Add the drained vegetables and tomato paste and cook briefly. Add the reserved marinade, water, prunes, salt and pepper and bring to a boil.
Cover and braise gently for 2½–3 hours, until the beef is tender. Add water if the pot becomes too dry.
Remove the beef, rosemary stems and cloves. Blend the sauce, slice the beef and return it to the sauce. Divide into 4 portions. Extra gnocchi is optional and is not included in these quantities.

name: Schnitzel with Potato Salad
description: Crispy breaded pork schnitzel served with warm Bavarian potato salad and lemon.

components.name: salt
components.comment: 1 g for pork; 2 g for salad

steps.text: Boil the potatoes until tender, about 20 minutes. Slice while warm. Toss with finely diced onion, vinegar, mustard, 15 ml oil, 2 g salt and pepper.
Pound the pork cutlets to about 5 mm thick and season with the remaining 1 g salt.
Put the flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs in separate dishes. Coat the cutlets in that order, shaking off excess. Discard unused coating that has touched raw pork.
Heat the remaining 135 ml oil in a wide pan. Shallow-fry the cutlets for 2–3 minutes on each side, until golden and cooked through. Drain well.
Serve each cutlet with half the potato salad and lemon juice.

name: Kartoffelsalat mit Würstchen (Potato Salad with Sausages)
description: Warm German potato salad dressed with broth and mustard, served with simply boiled sausages — an everyday family dinner.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, about 18 minutes. Drain, peel while warm, and slice.
Finely dice the onion and whisk with warm stock, vinegar, oil, mustard, salt, and pepper.
Pour the dressing over the warm sliced potatoes and toss gently. Let sit for 10 minutes to absorb the dressing.
Meanwhile, simmer the sausages in water for 8-10 minutes until heated through.
Scatter the potato salad with chives and serve alongside the sausages.

name: Spring Rolls
description: Rice paper rolls stuffed with vegetables, mint, rice vermicelli, and dipping sauce.

steps.text: Cook rice vermicelli according to package. Rinse in cold water and drain.
Julienne carrot and cucumber. Slice avocado.
Fill a large bowl with warm water. Dip one rice paper wrapper for 10–15 seconds until pliable.
Lay wrapper on a damp surface. Place herbs first, then noodles and vegetables on the lower third.
Fold the bottom up, fold sides in, and roll tightly forward.
Serve with a dipping sauce made from hoisin sauce, peanut butter, lime juice, and water.

name: Yaichnitsa (Russian Fried Eggs)
description: Simple everyday fried eggs the way they're made in most Russian kitchens — quick, no fuss, eaten straight from the pan.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a frying pan over medium heat until it starts to foam.
Crack the eggs directly into the pan, keeping the yolks whole.
Season with salt and pepper. Cook uncovered for 3-4 minutes until whites are set but yolks are still runny.
Slide onto plates, scatter with chopped green onion if using, and serve immediately with bread.

name: Grechka s Myasom (Buckwheat with Beef)
description: Everyday Russian dinner of nutty buckwheat kasha simmered with browned beef and onion — the kind of meal nobody needs a recipe for.

steps.text: Rinse the buckwheat under cold water until it runs clear.
Finely dice the onion and grate the carrot.
Heat oil in a deep pan and fry the onion and carrot until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add the beef mince, breaking it up, and cook until browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the buckwheat, then add water, salt, and the bay leaf.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low heat for 15-18 minutes until the buckwheat is tender and water is absorbed.
Remove the bay leaf, fluff with a fork, and let it rest covered for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Mercimek Çorbası (Red Lentil Soup)
description: Smooth Turkish red lentil soup with cumin, paprika butter drizzle, and lemon.

steps.text: Sauté diced onion and carrot in oil until soft. Add garlic and cumin.
Add rinsed red lentils and cover with vegetable stock. Bring to boil.
Simmer 20–25 minutes until lentils are completely soft and falling apart.
Blend until smooth. Adjust consistency with water.
Make topping: melt butter, add paprika and red pepper flakes — it should sizzle and turn red.
Serve soup with a drizzle of spiced butter, a squeeze of lemon, and croutons.

name: Baked Chicken with Potatoes
description: Whole chicken legs roasted with potatoes, garlic, and rosemary until golden.

steps.text: Score chicken legs and rub with olive oil, garlic, paprika, rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Cut potatoes into wedges and toss in olive oil with salt and herbs.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Arrange potatoes in a baking tray, place chicken on top.
Roast for 50–60 minutes, turning potatoes halfway, until chicken skin is crispy and golden.
Check chicken is cooked through (juices run clear). Rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Pad Thai
description: Thai-style stir-fried rice noodles with shrimp, egg, tamarind sauce and peanuts.

steps.text: Soak the rice noodles for about 30 minutes, or according to their packet instructions, then drain.
Mix the fish sauce, tamarind, sugar, oyster sauce and 2 tablespoons water.
Heat the oil in a wok. Stir-fry the shrimp until almost cooked, push to one side and scramble the eggs in the same wok.
Add the drained noodles and sauce. Toss for 2–3 minutes, until the noodles are tender and the shrimp is cooked through. Add a little water if needed.
Fold in the bean sprouts and sliced green onion. Divide into 2 portions and top with chopped peanuts, chilli flakes and lime juice.

name: Tavë Kosi (Albanian Baked Lamb)
description: Albanian national dish: tender lamb baked in a thick egg and yogurt custard.

steps.text: Cut lamb into pieces. Season and brown in butter on all sides until golden.
Add rice and enough water to cover. Parboil together for 10 minutes.
Transfer to a baking dish. Preheat oven to 190°C.
Whisk yogurt with eggs until completely smooth. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper.
Pour custard evenly over the lamb and rice.
Bake for 45 minutes until custard is set and golden on top. Serve straight from the dish.

name: Eggplant Parmigiana
description: Layers of fried aubergine, tomato sauce, and melted mozzarella baked until bubbly.

steps.text: Slice eggplant, salt it and leave for 20 minutes to draw out moisture. Pat dry.
Shallow-fry eggplant slices in olive oil until golden on both sides. Drain on paper towels.
Make a quick tomato sauce with canned tomatoes, garlic, and basil.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Layer eggplant, tomato sauce, and sliced mozzarella in a baking dish.
Repeat layers and finish with parmesan on top.
Bake for 30–35 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

name: Lamb Kleftiko
description: Slow-baked Greek lamb sealed in parchment with lemon, garlic, and herbs.

steps.text: Score lamb deeply and push garlic cloves and oregano into the cuts.
Marinate in lemon juice, olive oil, and oregano for 2–4 hours.
Place lamb on a large piece of baking parchment with sliced potato, tomato, and chunks of feta.
Fold parchment tightly to seal, creating a parcel. Secure with string.
Bake at 160°C for 3 hours. The lamb should be completely tender and falling off the bone.
Open parcel at the table to release the aromatic steam. Serve with crusty bread.

name: Mushroom Cream Soup
description: Velvety blended mushroom soup with cream, garlic, and fresh thyme.

steps.text: Sauté diced onion and garlic in butter until soft.
Add sliced mushrooms and cook on high heat until all moisture has evaporated and mushrooms are golden.
Add vegetable stock and fresh thyme. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Remove the thyme. Blend soup until completely smooth.
Return to pan, add cream, and heat gently. Season with salt and pepper. Garnish with a swirl of cream and sautéed mushroom slice.

name: Manti (Turkish Dumplings)
description: Tiny Turkish beef dumplings topped with garlic yogurt and spiced butter.

steps.text: Make stiff egg dough. Knead well and rest 30 minutes.
Mix beef mince with grated onion, salt, and pepper.
Roll dough very thin. Cut into tiny 3x3 cm squares.
Place a tiny piece of filling (the size of a hazelnut) on each square. Pinch all four corners to the centre to seal.
Boil in salted water for 8–10 minutes until dough is tender.
Serve with garlic yogurt, and a drizzle of butter melted with paprika and dried mint.

name: Egg and Bacon Toast
description: Fried egg and crispy bacon on buttered toast — a simple and satisfying classic.

steps.text: Fry bacon in a dry pan until crispy. Remove and set aside.
Toast bread until golden. Butter generously.
In the same pan with a little bacon fat, fry an egg sunny-side up. Season with salt and pepper.
Place bacon on toast, top with the fried egg. Serve immediately.

name: Falafel
description: Crisp chickpea falafel with fresh herbs, garlic, cumin and coriander.

components.name: sunflower oil
components.comment: frying bath; most is not consumed

steps.text: Soak the dried chickpeas in plenty of cold water in the refrigerator for at least 12 hours. Drain thoroughly. Do not use canned or cooked chickpeas.
Process the soaked chickpeas with the herbs, garlic, onion, cumin, coriander and salt to a fine, crumbly mixture. Do not purée.
Stir in the baking soda, cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Shape into 12 small balls.
Heat the frying oil to 180°C in a suitable deep pan. Fry in small batches for 3–4 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Drain well.
Serve 4 falafel per portion. Extra bread, salad or sauce is optional and is not included in the quantities.

name: Pea and Ham Soup
description: Thick and hearty split pea soup slowly simmered with a smoked ham hock.

steps.text: Soak split peas in cold water for 1 hour. Drain.
Place ham hock in a large pot with water. Bring to boil and simmer 1 hour.
Remove hock. Add drained peas, diced onion, carrot, celery, bay leaf, and thyme to the broth.
Simmer for 45 minutes until peas are completely soft and soup is thick.
Shred ham from the hock and return to the soup.
Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper. Serve with bread rolls.

name: Aloo Sabzi with Roti
description: Dry-spiced potato curry with warm flatbread — a quick, everyday North Indian home meal.

steps.text: Peel and dice the potatoes into small cubes.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them sizzle, then add diced onion and cook until soft.
Add the diced tomato, turmeric, and garam masala, cooking until the tomato breaks down.
Add the potatoes and a splash of water, cover, and cook on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender.
Season with salt, scatter with cilantro, and serve hot with warmed flatbread.

name: Dal-Chawal (Everyday Lentils and Rice)
description: The daily meal in most Indian households — simple turmeric lentils simmered soft, served over steamed rice.

steps.text: Rinse the lentils and rice separately. Cook the rice according to package instructions and set aside.
Simmer the lentils with turmeric and 500ml water in a pot until soft, about 15 minutes, skimming any foam.
Meanwhile, dice the onion and tomato, and mince the garlic and ginger.
Heat ghee in a small pan, fry the cumin seeds until fragrant, then add onion, garlic, and ginger, cooking until golden.
Add the tomato and cook until soft, then pour this tempering into the cooked lentils.
Season with salt, simmer 5 more minutes, and serve over rice, topped with cilantro.

name: Spanakopita (Greek Spinach and Feta Pie)
description: Crisp layers of filo wrapped around spinach and feta — a well-loved Greek savory pie, baked in home kitchens as a main course or side.

steps.text: Finely chop the onion and sauté in a little olive oil until soft, about 5 minutes.
Wilt the spinach in batches in the same pan, then drain well and squeeze out excess liquid once cool enough to handle.
Chop the spinach and mix with the onion, crumbled feta, eggs, dill, and salt.
Brush a baking dish with olive oil and layer half the filo sheets, brushing each with oil.
Spread the spinach filling evenly, then top with the remaining filo sheets, brushing each with oil.
Score the top into portions and bake at 180°C (350°F) for 35-40 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.
Let rest for 10 minutes before cutting and serving.

name: Grilled Octopus
description: Charred Mediterranean octopus with olive oil, lemon, and fresh oregano.

steps.text: Simmer octopus with a cork (supposedly tenderises it), bay leaf, and peppercorns for 40–60 minutes until tender when pierced.
Cool in the cooking liquid. Drain and pat dry.
Brush with olive oil. Grill on a very hot barbecue or griddle for 3–4 minutes per side until charred.
Slice tentacles. Drizzle with olive oil, lemon juice, and red wine vinegar.
Season with salt, dried oregano, and fresh parsley. Serve with crusty bread.

name: Patatas Bravas
description: Spanish fried potato cubes served with smoky spicy brava sauce and aioli.

steps.text: Cube potatoes. Par-boil for 5 minutes. Drain and dry well.
Deep-fry or roast at 220°C in plenty of oil until golden and crispy.
Make brava sauce: fry garlic in oil, add smoked paprika and cayenne, then canned tomatoes and a splash of vinegar. Simmer 10 minutes. Blend smooth.
Pile potatoes on a plate. Spoon brava sauce over generously.
Optionally add aioli (garlic mayo). Serve hot as a tapa.

name: Roasted Beet and Feta Salad
description: Earthy roasted beetroot with creamy feta, walnuts, and balsamic honey dressing.

steps.text: Wrap whole beets in foil and roast at 200°C for 45–50 minutes until tender. Cool and peel.
Slice or quarter beets. Toast walnuts in a dry pan.
Make dressing: whisk balsamic vinegar, honey, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Arrange rocket on plates. Add beets and crumbled feta.
Scatter walnuts over. Drizzle with dressing and serve immediately.

name: Sütlaç (Turkish Baked Rice Pudding)
description: Creamy Turkish baked rice pudding with a golden caramelised top.

steps.text: Boil rice in a small amount of water until soft. Drain.
Combine cooked rice with milk, sugar, and vanilla in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Mix cornstarch with a splash of cold milk. Stir into the pudding.
Cook, stirring constantly, for 15 minutes until thick and creamy.
Pour into individual oven-safe bowls. Bake at 200°C for 8–10 minutes until top is spotty golden brown.
Cool to room temperature, refrigerate until cold. Dust with cinnamon to serve.

name: Nalesniki (Polish Pancakes with Farmer's Cheese)
description: Thin Polish pancakes rolled around sweetened farmer's cheese — a favorite everyday breakfast or light dinner in Polish homes.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, and salt together until smooth, forming a thin batter.
Heat a little oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat and pour in a thin layer of batter, swirling to coat the pan.
Cook for about a minute until the edges lift, flip, and cook the other side briefly.
Repeat with the remaining batter, stacking the pancakes as you go.
Mix the farmer's cheese with sugar until well combined.
Spoon the cheese filling onto each pancake, roll up, and warm briefly in butter in a pan before serving.

name: Greek Salad
description: Chunky salad of cucumber, tomato, feta, olives, and oregano with olive oil.

steps.text: Chop cucumber and tomato into large chunks. Thinly slice red onion.
Combine in a bowl with Kalamata olives.
Drizzle generously with olive oil. Season with salt and dried oregano.
Place a thick slab of feta on top (traditional style). Serve without tossing.

name: Baked Trout
description: Whole trout roasted with herbs, lemon slices, and garlic until flaky and fragrant.

steps.text: Score both sides of the fish with 3 diagonal cuts. Season inside and out with salt and pepper.
Stuff the cavity with lemon slices, garlic, and fresh herbs.
Drizzle with olive oil and place in a baking dish or on a sheet of foil.
Roast at 200°C for 20–25 minutes until skin is crispy and flesh flakes easily.
Serve with extra lemon wedges and a fresh green salad.

name: Palak Paneer
description: Indian cottage cheese cubes in a vibrant spiced spinach and cream sauce.

steps.text: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes, drain and blend to a purée.
Cut the paneer into cubes. Heat the oil in a pan and lightly brown the paneer. Transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, soften diced onion for 8 minutes. Add chopped garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and garam masala and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the spinach, cream and salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return the paneer and heat through. Divide into 3 portions. Extra rice or bread is optional and is not included in the quantities.

name: Pizza Margherita
description: Classic Neapolitan pizza with tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella, and basil.

steps.text: Preheat oven to maximum temperature (250°C / 480°F) with a baking stone or tray inside.
Stretch the dough by hand into a thin round on a floured surface.
Spread a thin layer of crushed tomato sauce, leaving a border for the crust.
Tear mozzarella into pieces and distribute evenly over the sauce.
Slide pizza onto the hot stone and bake for 8–10 minutes until crust is charred at edges.
Remove from oven, scatter fresh basil leaves and drizzle with olive oil. Serve hot.

name: Samosa
description: Crispy fried pastry triangles stuffed with spiced potato and peas.

steps.text: Make pastry: rub oil into flour until crumbly. Add just enough cold water to form a stiff dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Boil potatoes, mash roughly. Fry cumin seeds in oil, add ginger and chili, then potatoes, peas, and spices. Cool.
Divide dough into balls. Roll each into a thin oval. Cut in half.
Form each half into a cone, fill with potato mixture, and seal the open edge tightly with water.
Deep-fry at 170°C for 5–6 minutes until golden and crispy. Serve with mint chutney and tamarind sauce.

name: Bruschetta
description: Toasted ciabatta rubbed with garlic and topped with diced tomato and fresh basil.

steps.text: Slice ciabatta and toast under a grill or in a hot pan until golden on both sides.
Rub each slice immediately with a halved raw garlic clove.
Dice ripe tomatoes and mix with torn basil, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spoon the tomato mixture onto the toast and serve immediately.

name: Pkhali (Georgian Walnut Vegetable Pâté)
description: Cooked vegetables finely minced with walnuts, garlic, and herbs into a dense, spreadable pâté — a cold side dish on almost every Georgian table.

steps.text: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, then drain and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Finely chop the spinach or pulse briefly in a food processor.
Crush the walnuts and garlic together into a coarse paste, either by hand with a mortar or in a food processor.
Mix the walnut paste with the spinach, vinegar, cilantro, khmeli-suneli, and salt until well combined.
Shape into small patties or a mound, garnish with pomegranate molasses or seeds, and chill briefly before serving with bread.

name: Eggs Benedict
description: Poached eggs on toasted English muffin with Canadian bacon and hollandaise sauce.

steps.text: Make hollandaise: whisk egg yolks over a bain-marie with a splash of white wine vinegar until thick. Slowly drizzle in clarified butter while whisking. Season with lemon juice and salt.
Bring water to a gentle simmer in a deep pan. Add a splash of vinegar.
Crack each egg into a cup. Create a gentle whirlpool in the water and slide egg in. Poach 3–4 minutes.
Pan-fry Canadian bacon. Toast English muffin halves.
Assemble: muffin → bacon → poached egg → hollandaise. Season and serve immediately.

name: Lobio (Georgian Bean Stew)
description: Kidney beans stewed with onion, walnuts, and cilantro — a hearty, everyday Georgian dish enjoyed with cornbread.

steps.text: If using dried beans, ensure they've been soaked overnight, then boil until tender, about 40 minutes; canned beans can be used directly, drained and rinsed.
Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat oil in a pan and cook the onion until soft and golden, about 8 minutes.
Crush the walnuts finely and add to the pan along with garlic and khmeli-suneli, stirring for a minute.
Add the cooked beans with a little of their cooking liquid, and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing some beans for a thicker texture.
Season with salt, stir in the cilantro, and serve warm.
